The role holds `EXECUTE` on those two functions and\n   nothing else; the gateway, reporter, memory and console roles are refused as recorders, and a\n   recorder is refused as any of them. **No KEK on the node for this.** `cp-manage node backup-check`\n   keeps the settings half on the control plane and joins the node's latest recorded repository\n   half; a node with no fresh repository report is not ready.\n3. **Two repositories, neither on the node, both encrypted by pgBackRest** (`aes-256-cbc`, one\n   passphrase per repository, generated on the node):\n   - **repo1: SFTP to a VM on the owner's second Proxmox server, at another site.** Fast restores\n     that do not depend on a provider. Its own account, key-only, chrooted to the repository path.\n   - **repo2: Cloudflare R2**, free tier (10 GB, no egress charge). A bucket token scoped to that\n     bucket alone, placed on the node by the owner.\n\n   Every backup and all WAL go to both (pgBackRest's multi-repository archiving). Readiness,\n   retention and ADR-064 are checked **per repository**; both must pass. Retention is by time and\n   covers the longest window any plan sells (ADR-068), with `repo*-retention-archive` set.\n4. **`archive_mode = on`** on the node, which restarts its PostgreSQL once — scheduled, stated, and\n   done before signups open, while the only tenant is the owner's.\n5. **The control plane backs itself up nightly** (`cp-manage control-plane backup`, ADR-070) and ships\n   the file to the same two destinations under a separate prefix, encrypted before it leaves the\n   host with a key that is **not** the KEK. ## 🤖 Claude

Slice 7 needs an architecture decision before any building, so I've written it up as ADR-086 in PR #214 (docs only): https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/214. It uses your two choices: a VM on your second Proxmox server at the other site, and Cloudflare R2's free tier.

**Why it isn't just configuration**
- **Where backups run:** `cp-manage node backup` runs pgBackRest where the control-plane database is. Neither of our machines has both pgBackRest with the data and write access to that database.
- **One repository only:** the backup code only understands a single repository, so two means code changes.
- **Node settings:** `archive_mode` is off on the node, and turning it on means restarting its PostgreSQL once.
- **Nothing else is copied:** nothing backs up the control plane, and customer files in SeaweedFS still exist as one copy.

**What ADR-086 proposes**
1. **Backups run on the node** on a timer, as `postgres`: a daily full backup plus differentials every 6 hours. Results are recorded through a role that can only call two functions for its own node, the same pattern as the health reporter. The node gets no KEK.
2. **Two repositories, neither on the node, both encrypted by pgBackRest.**
   - **repo1** is SFTP to the VM at the other site.
   - **repo2** is R2.
   - Every backup and all the WAL go to both, and each one is checked separately.
3. **`archive_mode = on`:** one restart of the node's PostgreSQL, scheduled with you, before signups open.
4. **The control plane** is dumped nightly, encrypted, and shipped to both destinations.
5. **Customer files** get a nightly `rclone sync` from SeaweedFS to a second R2 bucket.
6. **Restore** stays an attended command run on the node. That's a documented exception to ADR-083, which ruled out a standing process with control-plane access on the node, not a one-off run.
7. **Preflight** fails on a failed or stale backup check, instead of passing a node just because a stanza name is recorded (finding 21).

The plan now splits slice 7 into 7a–7e: the recording role, the node runner, the two repositories, the control plane plus files, and the restore test.

**What I need from you**
- **Accept or change ADR-086.** The open points are the node-side runner and recording role, the rclone copy of files, and the restore exception.
- **H-3 setup:**
  - **VM at the other site.** Can node .172 reach it over SSH (site-to-site VPN, or a public address with a port open)? Tell me how, and whether you want me to set up its backup account over SSH.
  - **R2.** Create two buckets (backups, files) and an API token scoped to each. You'll place the tokens on the node yourself; I'll give you the exact file and commands.
  - **KEK copy.** This is still unanswered: where the KEK and staff key live off both hosts. A password manager is the simple choice, as long as it holds neither backup credential.

--
-- Placement refuses a node without a health report newer than
-- `nodes.HEALTH_STALE_AFTER`, and until now the only writer was `cp-manage node
-- health`, which needs the control plane's own database role and the KEK -- so it
-- could not run on the node it describes, and the runbook named nothing to run it.
--
-- **Identity is a mapping column, as `nodes.gateway_role` is, and that is safe here
-- for the reason 0046 gives against it elsewhere.** A mapping is dangerous when a
-- narrowed role can write it. The gateway's grant revokes everything on `nodes` and
-- gives back UPDATE on `last_health_at` alone; the memory worker and embedder read
-- `nodes` and write nothing. Only the control plane's own role, through
-- `cp-manage node reporter grant`, writes this column.
ALTER TABLE nodes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS health_reporter_role TEXT UNIQUE;

COMMENT ON COLUMN nodes.health_reporter_role IS
    'The login role whose reports this node accepts (ADR-080). Written only by '
    'cp-manage node reporter grant.';

-- **No table privilege at all.** The reporter's role is granted EXECUTE on this and
-- USAGE on the schema, nothing else, so a stolen reporter password marks one node
-- fresh and reports its disk -- it reads no row, and writes no other column.
--
-- SECURITY DEFINER, so the body runs as the owner and needs no grant on `nodes`.
-- Which node is decided by `session_user`: inside a definer function
-- `current_user` is the owner, and `session_user` is the role that logged in.
-- Only a superuser can change it (SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION), and a superuser
-- already has the table.
--
-- The report *merges*: `metrics_json` also carries what `node realtime-check` and
-- `node backup-check` recorded, and a health report must not erase it. Only the

-- able to report itself fresh for ever.

    RETURNS TEXT
    LANGUAGE plpgsql

    SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp

DECLARE
    reported TEXT;

        RAISE EXCEPTION 'free disk must be a non-negative number of bytes'
            USING ERRCODE = '22023';

    IF reported IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'role % reports health for no node; run cp-manage node reporter grant', session_user
            USING ERRCODE = '42501';
    END IF;
    RETURN reported;
END
$$;

-- Phase 11 slice 1 (ADR-067, ADR-064): where a node's backups are recorded,
-- and what the platform believes about them.
--
-- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` has reserved "backup metadata later" since Phase 01.
-- This is later. The shape follows from two slice-0 findings rather than from
-- what a backup table usually looks like, and both are recorded here because
-- the columns are otherwise hard to justify:
--
--  1. **An untuned pgBackRest backup of an idle cluster waits forever.** Its
--     default begins after the next *regular* checkpoint and PostgreSQL skips
--     timed checkpoints when no WAL has been written -- measured at 15+ minutes
--     at 0% CPU with `num_timed = 0` after forty minutes of uptime. That is the
--     free tier's exact shape (ADR-022), so the nightly backup of a node full
--     of sleeping projects hangs rather than fails: no error, no exit code, and
--     nothing in the repository the next morning. A row is therefore written
--     when a backup *starts*, not when it finishes, and `running` is a state
--     the verification pass can age out. A table that only recorded successes
--     could not tell "hung since Tuesday" from "never ran".
--
--  2. **The repository is the durable record; this table is not.** These rows
--     say what the platform did and what it saw. They are not evidence that a
--     restorable backup exists -- only the repository is that, and only a
--     restore proves it (slice 2). Nothing here should ever be read as a
--     durability guarantee, which is why there is no `verified` flag: this
--     slice has no honest way to set one.

-- Which pgBackRest stanza covers this node's cluster. NULL means the node has
-- not been prepared for backup, which is a reportable state rather than an
-- error -- see `backup.BackupReadiness`.
--
-- One stanza per node, because a stanza owns a whole cluster and ADR-002 puts
-- every tenant of a node in one cluster. Per-tenant granularity is a restore
-- concern (slice 2), not a repository one.
ALTER TABLE nodes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backup_stanza TEXT;

-- How old the most recent completed backup may be before the maintenance pass
-- calls it a failure. NULL falls back to `backup.DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_HOURS`.
--
-- Configuration rather than a constant in application logic, per AGENTS.md: a
-- node backed up hourly and a node backed up weekly are both legitimate, and
-- the deployment knows which it is.
ALTER TABLE nodes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backup_max_age_hours INTEGER;

ALTER TABLE nodes
    ADD CONSTRAINT nodes_backup_max_age_positive
    CHECK (backup_max_age_hours IS NULL OR backup_max_age_hours > 0);


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS node_backups (
    id                BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    node_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Denormalised from `nodes.backup_stanza` on purpose. A stanza can be
    -- renamed or a node re-prepared against a different repository, and a
    -- history that silently re-labels its own past is worse than no history:
    -- this column says which repository the row was actually written against.
    stanza            TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- pgBackRest's three. `full` is self-contained; `diff` and `incr` are not,
    -- and a restore needs the chain -- which is why age is measured against a
    -- *full* backup separately from against any backup at all.
    backup_type       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (backup_type IN ('full', 'diff', 'incr')),

    -- pgBackRest's own label, e.g. `20260826-143012F`. NULL while running,
    -- because it is not assigned until the backup completes. It is the join
    -- key back to the repository, and the only identifier that means anything
    -- to `pgbackrest restore --set=`.
    label             TEXT,

    started_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- `running` is a first-class outcome here, not a transient. See note 1

"""A node reports its own health as a role that can do nothing else (ADR-080).

Found by the deployment rehearsal: placement needs a fresh health report and
nothing in the runbook could send one from a node. What is held here:

- **the reporter's role reads nothing and writes nothing** but the one function;
- **it reports for its own node only**, decided by the login role in the database,
  and an unmapped role is refused rather than reporting for nobody silently;
- **a report merges**: what realtime-check and backup-check recorded survives it
  (the old `node health` erased both);
- **the time is the database's**, and a reported node becomes placeable;
- **the grant refuses roles that must not report**: a gateway role, a role that
  cannot log in, a role already reporting for another node;
- **the reporter stays silent while local PostgreSQL does not answer**.
"""

PASSWORD = "reporter-test-only-4c1d"  # noqa: S105 - a throwaway role in a scratch database
GATEWAY = "mldb_test_reporter_gateway"


def _drop(conn, role: str) -> None:
    exists = db.one(conn, "SELECT 1 AS ok FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = %s", (role,))
    if exists:
        conn.execute(f'REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.report_node_health(bigint) FROM "{role}"')
        conn.execute(f'REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM "{role}"')
        conn.execute(f'DROP ROLE "{role}"')

        conn.commit()

    def login(role: str) -> psycopg.Connection:
        parts = psycopg.conninfo.conninfo_to_dict(migrated_database)
        parts.update(user=role, password=PASSWORD)
        return psycopg.connect(psycopg.conninfo.make_conninfo(**parts), autocommit=True)

    try:
        yield login
    finally:
        with db.connection() as conn:
            conn.execute("UPDATE nodes SET health_reporter_role = NULL")
            for role in (REPORTER, OTHER):
                _drop(conn, role)
            conn.commit()


def _grant(role: str = REPORTER, node: str = "rep-node") -> int:
    return manage._cmd_node_reporter_grant(argparse.Namespace(role=role, node=node))

def free_disk_bytes(path: str) -> int:
    """Bytes available to an unprivileged writer, as `df` reports them."""
    stats = os.statvfs(path)
    return stats.f_bavail * stats.f_frsize


def local_postgres_answers(conninfo: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the node's cluster is accepting connections. PQping authenticates nothing, so
    no credential is needed; PQPING_REJECT is a server in startup, shutdown or recovery, which
    cannot take a project either."""
    return pq.PGconn.ping(conninfo.encode()) == pq.Ping.OK


def report_once(settings: Settings, *, connect=psycopg.connect) -> str | None:
    """Send one report. Returns the node reported for, or None when nothing was sent."""
    if not local_postgres_answers(settings.local_postgres):
        log.warning("local PostgreSQL is not answering; not reporting, so placement stops choosing this node")
        return None
    free = free_disk_bytes(settings.data_directory)
    with connect(settings.database_url, connect_timeout=10, autocommit=True) as conn:
        node = conn.execute("SELECT public.report_node_health(%s)", (free,)).fetchone()[0]
    log.info("reported health for %s: free_disk_bytes=%d", node, free)
    return node


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="maludb-node-reporter", description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="send one report and exit (0 sent, 1 not)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    cp_logging.configure()
    settings = Settings.from_environment()

    if args.once:
        try:
            return 0 if report_once(settings) else 1
        except psycopg.Error as exc:
            # The type and the server's message; never the DSN.
            log.error("report failed: %s: %s", type(exc).__name__, (exc.diag.message_primary or "").strip())
            return 1

    stopping = False

    def stop(signum, _frame) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001 - signal handler signature
        nonlocal stopping
        stopping = True

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    while not stopping:
        try:
            report_once(settings)
        except psycopg.Error as exc:
            log.error("report failed: %s: %s", type(exc).__name__, (exc.diag.message_primary or "").strip())
        except OSError as exc:
            log.error("report failed: %s", exc)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + settings.interval_seconds
        while not stopping and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(1)

Written only by `cp-manage node\n-- backup-recorder grant`, as the control plane's own role.\nALTER TABLE nodes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backup_recorder_role TEXT UNIQUE;\n\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN nodes.backup_recorder_role IS\n    'The login role whose backup records this node accepts (ADR-086). Written only by '\n    'cp-manage node backup-recorder grant.';\n\n\n-- A backup is beginning. Written before pgBackRest runs, for 0026's reason: a backup that\n-- never returns must leave a `running` row the maintenance pass can age out.\n--\n-- The stanza is the node's, never the caller's: a row claims the repository the control\n-- plane prepared, so a recorder cannot file backups of some other stanza against its node.\n-- One start a minute, so a looping or hostile runner cannot bury the one row the pass reads.\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.start_node_backup(p_backup_type TEXT)\n    RETURNS BIGINT\n    LANGUAGE plpgsql\n    SECURITY DEFINER\n    SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp\nAS $$\nDECLARE\n    node RECORD;\n    started BIGINT;\nBEGIN\n    SELECT id, name, backup_stanza INTO node\n      FROM public.nodes WHERE backup_recorder_role = session_user::text;\n    IF node.id IS NULL THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'role % records backups for no node; run cp-manage node backup-recorder grant', session_user\n            USING ERRCODE = '42501';\n    END IF;\n    IF node.backup_stanza IS NULL THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'node % has no stanza; run cp-manage node backup-check first', node.name\n            USING ERRCODE = '55000';\n    END IF;\n    IF p_backup_type IS NULL OR p_backup_type NOT IN ('full', 'diff', 'incr') THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'backup type must be full, diff or incr' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.node_backups\n                WHERE node_id = node.id AND started_at > now() - interval '1 minute') THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'node % started a backup less than a minute ago', node.name\n            USING ERRCODE = '55000';\n    END IF;\n    INSERT INTO public.node_backups (node_id, stanza, backup_type)\n         VALUES (node.id, node.backup_stanza, p_backup_type)\n      RETURNING id INTO started;\n    RETURN started;\nEND\n$$;\n\n\n-- A backup this recorder started has ended. Only a `running` row of its own node, so\n-- history cannot be rewritten: a failure stays a failure and a completed backup keeps the\n-- label it completed with. A completed row needs a label shaped like pgBackRest's, because\n-- the label is what `pgbackrest restore --set` is given and 0026 refuses a complete row\n-- without one.\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.finish_node_backup(\n    p_backup_id BIGINT,\n    p_status TEXT,\n    p_label TEXT,\n    p_database_bytes BIGINT,\n    p_repository_bytes BIGINT,\n    p_wal_start TEXT,\n    p_wal_stop TEXT,\n    p_error TEXT\n)\n    RETURNS VOID\n    LANGUAGE plpgsql\n    SECURITY DEFINER\n    SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp\nAS $$\nDECLARE\n    node_id_ INTEGER;\nBEGIN\n    SELECT id INTO node_id_ FROM public.nodes WHERE backup_recorder_role = session_user::text;\n    IF node_id_ IS NULL THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'role % records backups for no node; run cp-manage node backup-recorder grant', session_user\n            USING ERRCODE = '42501';\n    END IF;\n    IF p_status IS NULL OR p_status NOT IN ('complete', 'failed') THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'a finished backup is complete or failed' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    IF p_status = 'complete'\n       AND (p_label IS NULL OR p_label !~ '^[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}F(_[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}[DI])?$') THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'a complete backup needs a pgBackRest label' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    IF coalesce(p_database_bytes, 0) < 0 OR coalesce(p_repository_bytes, 0) < 0 THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'sizes must be non-negative' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    IF (p_wal_start IS NOT NULL AND p_wal_start !~ '^[0-9A-F]{24}$')\n       OR (p_wal_stop IS NOT NULL AND p_wal_stop !~ '^[0-9A-F]{24}$') THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'WAL segment names are 24 hexadecimal characters' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    UPDATE public.node_backups\n       SET status = p_status, finished_at = now(), label = p_label,\n           database_bytes = p_database_bytes, repository_bytes = p_repository_bytes,\n           wal_start = p_wal_start, wal_stop = p_wal_stop,\n           error = left(p_error, 2000)\n     WHERE id = p_backup_id AND node_id = node_id_ AND status = 'running';\n    IF NOT FOUND THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'no running backup % on this node', p_backup_id USING ERRCODE = '55000';\n    END IF;\nEND\n$$;\n\n\n-- The repository half of readiness, which only the node can see: `pgbackrest check`,\n-- `info`, and the repository options, per repository (ADR-086 decision 3). Merged into\n-- `metrics_json` under keys of its own, so it cannot overwrite what the control plane's\n-- `node backup-check` recorded about archive_mode and wal_level -- readiness joins the two.\n-- The time is the database's, for 0050's reason.\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_node_backup_check(p_report JSONB)\n    RETURNS TEXT\n    LANGUAGE plpgsql\n    SECURITY DEFINER\n    SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp\nAS $$\nDECLARE\n    recorded TEXT;\nBEGIN\n    IF p_report IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(p_report) <> 'object' THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'a repository report is a JSON object' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    IF octet_length(p_report::text) > 65536 THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'a repository report is at most 64 KiB' USING ERRCODE = '22023';\n    END IF;\n    UPDATE public.nodes\n       SET metrics_json = coalesce(metrics_json, '{}'::jsonb)\n                          || jsonb_build_object('backup_repository', p_report,\n                                                'backup_repository_checked_at', now(),\n                                                'backup_repository_reported_by', session_user::text)\n     WHERE backup_recorder_role = session_user::text\n    RETURNING name INTO recorded;\n    IF recorded IS NULL THEN\n        RAISE EXCEPTION 'role % records backups for no node; run cp-manage node backup-recorder grant', session_user\n            USING ERRCODE = '42501';\n    END IF;\n    RETURN recorded;\nEND\n$$;\n\nREVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.start_node_backup(TEXT) FROM PUBLIC;\nREVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.finish_node_backup(BIGINT, TEXT, TEXT, BIGINT, BIGINT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT) FROM PUBLIC;\nREVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.record_node_backup_check(JSONB) FROM PUBLIC;\n\nCOMMENT ON FUNCTION public.start_node_backup(TEXT) IS\n    'Open a running node_backups row for the node whose backup_recorder_role is session_user (ADR-086).';\nCOMMENT ON FUNCTION public.finish_node_backup(BIGINT, TEXT, TEXT, BIGINT, BIGINT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT) IS\n    'Close a running node_backups row of the recorder''s own node (ADR-086).';\nCOMMENT ON FUNCTION public.record_node_backup_check(JSONB) IS\n    'Merge the node-side repository check into metrics_json for the recorder''s own node (ADR-086).';\n"

    is off by default on every PostgreSQL cluster ever installed.

class RepositoryState:

    the same as a node with a broken repository and must not be reported as
    though it were -- the same distinction `realtime.NodeReadiness` draws for
    the physical-replication probe, and for the same reason.

    detail: str
    # From `pgbackrest check`, which validates the configuration end to end and
    # forces a WAL segment through the archive_command. This is the one call
    # that proves archiving works rather than that it is configured.

    check_detail: str = ""
    pg_path: str | None = None
    repo_path: str | None = None
    # Both halves of retention. Unset, pgBackRest warns on every run that the
    # repository may run out of space, and separately that archive logs will not
    # be expired -- both true, neither fatal, which is the problem.

    retention_archive: int | None = None

    # existing: a plan promises a window in *days*, and `repo1-retention-full`
    # is a count of full backups unless this says otherwise. A count cannot be
    # compared with a window without knowing the backup schedule, so a node left
    # on the default has a promise nothing can check -- which is reported as
    # unverifiable rather than passed.
    retention_full_type: str | None = None

    # repository can actually deliver, and they are different kinds of bound.
    # A 30-day promise on a repository three days old is a promise nothing can
    # keep, and an operator should be told which of the two refused a restore.

    newest_backup_at: datetime | None = None

    def earliest_recoverable_at(self) -> datetime | None:
        """The oldest point in time this repository can restore to.

        The *end* of the oldest backup, not its start: recovery replays forward
        from a consistent point, so a target before the oldest backup finished
        has nothing to replay onto. None when the repository holds no backups,
        which is not "unbounded" and must not be read as one.

        return self.oldest_backup_at

def _check_nodes(conn: psycopg.Connection, report: Report) -> None:
    rows = db.query(
        conn,
        """
        SELECT name, status, last_health_at, backup_stanza,
               last_health_at > now() - %s AS fresh
          FROM nodes
         ORDER BY name
        """,
        (nodes.HEALTH_STALE_AFTER,),
    )
    if not rows:
        report.add(
            "nodes",
            False,
            "none registered. Signup would succeed and the customer's first "
            "action -- creating a project -- would answer 503",
        )
        return

    placeable = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == nodes.PLACEABLE_STATUS and r["fresh"]]
    if not placeable:
        detail = "; ".join(
            f"{r['name']} is {r['status']}"
            + ("" if r["fresh"] else ", health stale")
            for r in rows
        )
        report.add("nodes", False, f"none can take a project: {detail}")
        return

    report.add(
        "nodes",
        True,
        f"{len(placeable)} of {len(rows)} placeable: "
        + ", ".join(r["name"] for r in placeable),
    )

    # Advisory rather than fatal: a node without a stanza serves traffic
    # perfectly and cannot be recovered, which is a decision an operator is
    # allowed to make and should not make silently.
    unbacked = [r["name"] for r in placeable if not r["backup_stanza"]]
    if unbacked:
        report.add(
            "node backups",
            False,
            "no pgBackRest stanza recorded for " + ", ".join(unbacked)
            + ". `cp-manage node backup-check --name <node> --stanza <stanza>` "
            "records one; until then these nodes cannot be recovered",
            advisory=True,
        )
    else:
        report.add("node backups", True, "every placeable node has a stanza")

def _read_config_lines(config_path: str, *, run_as: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """The configuration file's lines, read as whoever can actually read it.

    Mode 0600 owned by the cluster owner on a Debian/Ubuntu install, so the
    direct read is attempted first and the become-the-owner path is the
    fallback rather than the default -- a control plane that can read the file
    should not shell out to do it.
    """
    try:
        with open(config_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return handle.readlines()
    except PermissionError:
        user = DEFAULT_RUN_AS if run_as is None else run_as
        if not user:
            raise
        proc = _run(["sudo", "-n", "-u", checked_run_as(user), "cat", config_path])
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise
        return proc.stdout.splitlines()


# pgBackRest's whole vocabulary for this option. Anything else is not a value
# this module can reason about.
_RETENTION_TYPES = ("count", "time")


def _retention_type(value: str | None) -> str:
    """Normalise `repo1-retention-full-type` to something with two known values.

    Closed set rather than sanitised string, and the difference matters. This
    value comes out of an operator-editable file, and it reaches a terminal --
    `node backup-check`, `node backup-policy` -- and `capacity_json`. Slice 1's
    security review closed exactly this shape once already, for a stanza name
    reaching a subprocess argv and for `pgbackrest.conf` credentials reaching a
    printed dataclass. A length cap and an escape filter would be the weaker
    answer here: there are two legal values, so anything else is `unknown` and
    the platform says so.

    Absent means pgBackRest's default, which is `count`. Recorded as the
    effective value rather than as None, because for ADR-068's purposes a node
    never configured and a node configured to the default are the same node.
    `unknown` is deliberately *not* `count`: it means the file says something
    this module did not understand, and the ADR-068 check treats it the same way
    it treats a count -- as not checkable -- rather than guessing.
    """
    if value is None:
        return "count"
    normalised = value.strip().lower()
    return normalised if normalised in _RETENTION_TYPES else "unknown"


def _iso(when: datetime | None) -> str | None:
    """`capacity_json` is JSONB and json.dumps cannot carry a datetime."""
    return when.isoformat() if when is not None else None


def _int_or_none(value: str | None) -> int | None:
    try:
        return int(value) if value is not None else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _tail(text: str, limit: int = 400) -> str:
    """The end of a command's output, which is where pgBackRest puts the reason."""
    cleaned = " ".join((text or "").split())
    return cleaned[-limit:] if len(cleaned) > limit else cleaned

def test_a_healthy_node_passes(db_pool):  # noqa: ARG001
    _node()
    assert _named(_run(), "nodes").ok


def test_a_node_without_a_backup_stanza_warns_rather_than_fails(db_pool):  # noqa: ARG001
    """Serving without backups is a decision an operator may make.

    It must not be one they make silently, so it warns -- and a warning does not
    make `report.ok` false, because refusing to launch over it would be this
    tool overriding a choice that is not its own.
    """
    _plan("free")
    _node(stanza=None)
    report = _run()
    check = _named(report, "node backups")
    assert not check.ok
    assert check.advisory
    assert check in report.warnings
    assert check not in report.failures

## 🤖 Claude

Slice 7a is merged (#215, along with the ADR-086 docs in #214), and 7b is open as PR #216 (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/216). Neither is deployed yet.

**7b: the node's backup runner**
- **`node_backup.py`** runs on the node as `postgres`, with no keys (a test checks it never loads the KEK code).
  - **`full` / `diff`:** writes a running row through the recorder role, runs pgBackRest with `--start-fast`, and closes the row with pgBackRest's own label and sizes. A failure is recorded with its reason. A backup that hangs leaves the row running so the maintenance pass reports it.
  - **`check`:** inspects the repositories on the node and records a report.
- **The node's report is treated as untrusted input.** A report that's missing, over 26 hours old, or for the wrong stanza counts as "not examined", never as healthy.
  - The node decides whether a repository shares its disk. Run from the control plane, that check would have looked at the control plane's own disks and answered about the wrong host.
  - `cp-manage node backup-check` now combines the node's report with the cluster settings it reads remotely.
- **Units:**
  - a service template running as `postgres` with a 6-hour limit;
  - timers: a full backup daily at 02:15, differentials at 08:15, 14:15 and 20:15, and checks every six hours.
- **Preflight, finding 21:** a node now needs a passing backup check under a week old and a repository report under 26 hours old. That's a failure in production. A recorded stanza name used to be enough.
- **Tests:** 19 new; 294 pass across the backup, recorder, preflight, units, restore and maintenance suites.

**Deploying 7a**
It adds migration 0058, and after it the gateway grant must be re-run on the control plane. Until then preflight's "gateway role" check fails. I'll deploy it together with 7b once #216 is merged, unless you want 7a on the VMs sooner.

**Next is 7c**, the two repositories plus `archive_mode = on`. It's blocked on your H-3 setup:
1. **VM at the other site:** how can node .172 reach it over SSH, via a site-to-site VPN or a public address and port? And do you want me to create its backup account over SSH?
2. **R2:** two buckets, one for backups and one for files, each with an API token limited to that bucket. You'll place the tokens on the node yourself.
3. **KEK copy:** where the KEK and staff key will live, away from both hosts.
4. **Restart window:** turning on `archive_mode` restarts the node's PostgreSQL once. Tell me when that's acceptable.

**Node (.172)**

- `archive_mode` is off (turning it on needs a PostgreSQL restart);
- pgBackRest has no stanza configured;

- the repository is on the same disk as the data, which is a production failure under ADR-064.

**Preflight:** "node backups" now **fails** for these reasons, where it used to pass because a stanza name was recorded (finding 21). It stays failing until 7c is deployed and checked.

## 🤖 Claude

Restart window noted, so I'll do the node work now. One constraint shapes the order: `archive_mode = on` needs a **working** `archive_command`. With archiving on and nothing archiving, PostgreSQL keeps every WAL segment until the node's disk fills. The off-site repositories are still waiting on your H-3 setup, so the plan is:

1. **Interim local repository** (`/var/lib/pgbackrest` on the node), encrypted, with 14-day retention. It makes archiving and backups real today, but it doesn't meet ADR-086, and preflight will keep failing it as co-located, which is correct. It gets replaced once the other-site VM and R2 exist.
2. **`archive_mode = on`**, then restart the node's PostgreSQL once, create the stanza, run `pgbackrest check`, take the first full backup through the runner, and turn on the full and diff timers.
3. **Code for 7c:** readiness that understands several repositories (repo1, repo2), so the off-site repositories slot in without further code.

Checking the node before touching PostgreSQL.

    def failures(self) -> list[str]:
        """Why this node must not be relied on for backup. Empty means it may.

        Ordered by how expensive the fix is, following `realtime.NodeReadiness`:
        `archive_mode` is postmaster context, so changing it restarts the
        cluster and takes every tenant on the node down with it. A node that is
        going to fail on that should fail on it before anybody edits a
        repository path.
        """
        problems: list[str] = []

        if self.archive_mode not in ("on", "always"):
            problems.append(
                f"archive_mode is {self.archive_mode!r}; WAL is not archived, so there is no "
                "point in time to recover to and no backup is restorable past the moment it "
                "was taken. This is postmaster context: fixing it restarts the cluster"
            )

        if self.wal_level not in SUFFICIENT_WAL_LEVELS:
            problems.append(
                f"wal_level is {self.wal_level!r}, below 'replica'; the WAL a replay needs is "
                "not written at all. Also postmaster context"
            )

        if not self.archive_command.strip() or self.archive_command.strip() == "(disabled)":
            problems.append(
                "archive_command is empty; archive_mode is on and nothing is archiving"
            )

        # The archiver's own report, which is the difference between "configured"

                f"archived a segment (last failure: {self.archive_last_failed_wal}); "
                "WAL is accumulating in pg_wal and no backup taken here is restorable"
            )

        if self.repository.reachable and self.repository.check_ok is False:
            problems.append(
                f"`pgbackrest check` failed: {self.repository.check_detail}. The repository is "
                "configured and does not work, which is the state a nightly backup reports "
                "nothing about"

        if self.repository.reachable and self.repository.retention_full is None:
            problems.append(
                "repo1-retention-full is unset; pgBackRest keeps every backup forever and warns "

def _read_stanza_options(stanza: str, config_path: str, *, run_as: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The stanza's own section of pgbackrest.conf, plus the global section.

    Parsed rather than asked for, because pgBackRest has no command that prints
    its effective configuration. The same two-sources shape as
    `realtime`'s `pg_hba` handling: the probe (`pgbackrest check`) says whether
    it works, and the file says what it is, and a check that only did the first
    could not tell an operator that retention is unset.

    is unset" -- the conservative direction, and the fix is to write the option.

    **Only the five options this module reads are kept.** The file can hold
    `repo1-s3-key` and `repo1-s3-key-secret`, and there is no reason for a
    credential to be carried in a dict that later feeds a dataclass an operator

## 🤖 Claude

node-01 is now actually backed up: WAL archiving is on and the first full backup is taken and recorded. For now the backups sit in an interim repository on the node's own disk. The 7c code for the two off-site repositories is in PR #217 (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/217), not merged.

**What I did on node-01**
- **pgBackRest config:** I rewrote `/etc/pgbackrest.conf` (the old template is kept as `.orig`). It sets up the interim local repository, encrypted with a passphrase generated on the node, keeping 30 days.
- **Why a local repository first:** with `archive_mode` on, PostgreSQL keeps every WAL file until it's archived. Turning archiving on without a working destination would slowly fill the disk, and the off-site destinations are still waiting on your setup.
- **Archiving:** `archive_mode = on` with a 5-minute `archive_timeout`. PostgreSQL restarted once at 16:31 UTC and came straight back; the gateway, storage and reporter stayed up.
- **First backup:** the stanza is created and `pgbackrest check` passes. The full backup `20260917-163138F` shrank 63 MB to 6.4 MB in 20 seconds, and it was recorded through the recorder role.
- **Timers:** full, diff and check are all on. The next diff is at 20:15 UTC and the next full at 02:15.
- **Retention finding:** I first set 14 days. The check correctly refused it because the longest plan promises 30, so it's now 30.

**Status**
- `cp-manage node backups` shows node-01 **ok**.
- `backup-check` fails only because the repository is on the same disk as the data (ADR-064). That's correct until the off-site repositories replace it.
- The plan records the interim repository as a temporary exception to ADR-086.

**PR #217 (7c code)**
- **Every repository checked separately:** readiness reads repo1–repo4 (type, path, retention) and never the keys or passphrases. It checks retention, the 30-day promise and co-location for each one.
- **Bug fixed along the way:** co-location was judged by path alone. An SFTP repository's path is a path on the *other site's* machine, but it would have been checked against the node's own disks. S3 and SFTP repositories are now off-host by definition.
- **Production warning:** it warns while fewer than two repositories are off the host.
- **Runbook:** `deploy/pgbackrest.conf.example` sets repo1 to SFTP at the other site (pinned host fingerprint) and repo2 to R2, both encrypted, 30 days. A test checks the example passes production readiness as written, and DEPLOYMENT §2.8 has the step-by-step.
- **Tests:** 195 passed across the backup, recorder, runner, preflight and restore suites.

**To replace the interim repository, I need from you (H-3):**
1. **VM at the other site:** how node .172 reaches it over SSH, and whether I should create the `pgbackrest` account there.
2. **R2:** two buckets (backups, files) and a token limited to each. You place the tokens on the node yourself.
3. **Offline copy:** where the KEK, the staff key and the pgBackRest passphrases will live. The interim repository's passphrase exists only on the node right now.

Merging #217 is safe now: it's code and docs, and it changes nothing about how the node runs today. Slices 7d (control-plane dump and a copy of customer files to R2) and 7e (restore drills) come after H-3.

## 🤖 Claude

Understood. The node's backups stay in the local repository for now, and the VM and R2 are off the list. Before I change anything, two consequences you should know, because the checks were built to refuse exactly this:

1. **Preflight will fail until something changes.** In production, ADR-064 treats a repository on the same disk as the data as "not a backup". So "node backups" stays a hard FAIL, and slice 10's launch check needs no failures. Leaving it failing would train everyone to ignore preflight. Weakening the check silently would be worse.
2. **The risk is real, even though it's cheap to accept for a beta.** One lost disk or VM takes the database *and* its backups. Customer files (SeaweedFS) also have a single copy, and the control plane has no dump yet.

My proposal is to record this as an explicit, time-limited exception rather than bend the check. Drafting it as ADR-087.

<details><summary>🔧 Bash</summary>

```json
{
  "command": "git fetch -q origin && git worktree add -q -b docs/adr-087-local-backups /home/maludb/mpa-adr087 origin/main && cd /home/maludb/mpa-adr087 && cat >> docs/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'\n\n## ADR-087 — The free-tier beta keeps node backups on the node, as a named, time-boxed exception to ADR-064\n\nStatus: **Proposed** 2026-09-17. The owner decided to use local backups for now and not to set up the\nsecond-site VM or Cloudflare R2 (ADR-086 decision 3). The mechanism below needs acceptance. Related:\nADR-064 (a repository in the data's failure domain is not a backup), ADR-068 (recovery windows),\nADR-069 (object durability), ADR-070 (control-plane recovery), ADR-086 (two off-host repositories).\n\n**Context.** node-01 archives WAL and takes full and differential backups into a local, encrypted\nrepository with 30-day retention (free slice 7c). That protects against the failures a beta is most\nlikely to see: a customer's mistake (point-in-time restore), a bad migration, a corrupted table.\nIt does not protect against losing the node's disk or VM, which takes the database and its backups\ntogether. ADR-064 makes that a **production failure** in `node backup-check`, so preflight's \"node\nbackups\" fails for as long as the repository stays local, and slice 10's launch check requires a\npreflight with no failures.\n\nTwo ways to get past that were rejected: leaving preflight failing (a check that is always red is a\ncheck nobody reads, and the next real failure would hide behind it) and relaxing ADR-064 in code (a\nproduction control weakened by a line nobody reviews again).\n\n**Decision.**\n\n1. **Local repositories are allowed for the beta, per node, by an operator's recorded acceptance.**\n   `cp-manage node backup-accept-local --name <node> --until <date> --reason <text>` records who\n   accepted, why and until when. While it is in force, ADR-064's co-location failure for that node\n   becomes a **warning that names the acceptance and its expiry**; every other failure (archiving,\n   retention, `pgbackrest check`, the ADR-068 window) stays a failure.\n2. **At most 90 days, and it lapses by itself.** Expired, the failure returns. ## 🤖 Claude

Done. The VM and R2 are off the list, and node-01 keeps backing up locally: WAL archiving, a nightly full backup, differentials every six hours, 30 days kept, and encrypted. That covers the likeliest beta problems, like a customer's mistake, a bad migration or a corrupted table, through point-in-time restore. It does **not** cover losing the node's disk or VM, which takes the database and its backups together.

**The catch:** the production backup check treats a repository on the same disk as "not a backup" (ADR-064). So preflight's "node backups" would stay a hard FAIL forever and block the launch check.

**ADR-087, proposed in PR #218** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/218), records your decision as an explicit exception rather than weakening the check:
- **A per-node acceptance** you run with `cp-manage node backup-accept-local --name node-01 --until <date> --reason <text>`. While it's in force, only the same-disk failure becomes a warning naming who accepted it, why, and until when. Archiving, retention, `pgbackrest check` and the 30-day window still fail if they break.
- **At most 90 days,** and it lapses by itself; renewing means recording a new decision.
- **Preflight shows the acceptance,** so anyone reading it knows host-loss recovery isn't available.
- The launch plan records that the off-site targets are deferred (H-3).

**Still to know**
- **Customer files** in SeaweedFS remain a single copy.
- **Slice 9** (the public site and terms) must not promise backups beyond this.
- **PR #217** (the 7c code for multiple repositories) is still worth merging. It also makes the local repository check precise, and the off-site setup can be added later without code changes.

**Next, once you accept ADR-087:**
1. Build the acceptance command and run it for node-01, so preflight passes with the named warning.
2. **7d:** a nightly control-plane dump on the control-plane VM. It's a different VM from the node, so losing one doesn't take both.
3. **7e:** a point-in-time restore drill of one free project from the local repository, which is what proves the backups actually work.

Say "accept ADR-087" (and whether to merge #217 and #218), and I'll build it.

# The control plane's half of the maintenance pass (ADR-083), run by maludb-maintenance.timer.
#
# Every pass except sleeping idle workers: retries, billing grace and reconciliation (ADR-051,
# ADR-053 -- without this, purchases are recorded and never applied), storage and object
# measurement and enforcement, and the capacity, slot, backup and drift checks. It loads the KEK
# and reaches node admin credentials, so it runs where the provisioner does and as that user.
#
# `--skip sleep`: each node sleeps its own workers as its gateway (maludb-node-maintenance), because
# the per-project units exist only on the node.

[Unit]
Description=MaluDB maintenance pass (control plane)
Documentation=file:///opt/maludb/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md
Wants=postgresql.service
After=postgresql.service network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=maludb-provisioner
Group=maludb-provisioner
EnvironmentFile=/etc/maludb/provisioner.env
LoadCredential=kek:/etc/maludb/keys/kek
LoadCredential=pepper:/etc/maludb/keys/pepper
ExecStart=/opt/maludb/.venv/bin/python -m services.control_plane.manage maintenance run --skip sleep
WorkingDirectory=/opt/maludb
# A pass over many projects can run long; the timer does not start a second one meanwhile.
TimeoutStartSec=15min

NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectSystem=strict
# tmpfs, not true: libpq looks for ~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt on every TLS
# connection and tolerates ENOENT but not the EACCES that `true` returns.
ProtectHome=tmpfs
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
ReadOnlyPaths=/opt/maludb /etc/maludb
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX
RestrictNamespaces=true
LockPersonality=true
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true
[Unit]
Description=MaluDB maintenance pass (control plane), every minute

[Timer]
OnBootSec=2min
OnUnitInactiveSec=1min
AccuracySec=10s
Unit=maludb-maintenance.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

Other files are ignored.\"\"\"\n    found = []\n    for name in os.listdir(directory):\n        if not (name.startswith(DUMP_PREFIX) and name.endswith(DUMP_SUFFIX)):\n            continue\n        stamp = name[len(DUMP_PREFIX):-len(DUMP_SUFFIX)]\n        try:\n            taken = datetime.strptime(stamp, \"%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ\").replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        found.append((taken, os.path.join(directory, name)))\n    return sorted(found)\n\n\ndef prune_dumps(directory: str, *, keep_days: int, now: datetime | None = None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Remove dumps older than `keep_days`, never the newest one. Returns what was removed.\n\n    Called only after a new dump succeeded, so a run of failing nights keeps the last good file\n    rather than pruning the directory empty.\n    \"\"\"\n    if keep_days < 1:\n        raise ValueError(\"keep at least one day of dumps\")\n    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)\n    dumps = dumps_in(directory)\n    removed = []\n    for taken, path in dumps[:-1]:\n        if now - taken > timedelta(days=keep_days):\n            os.remove(path)\n            removed.append(path)\n    return removed\n\n\n'''\nassert anchor in s; s=s.replace(anchor, add+anchor,1)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -n \"^from datetime\\|^import os\" services/control_plane/recovery.py",

## 🤖 Claude

ADR-087 is accepted and #217 is merged. #218 conflicted with #217 in the plan file, so I rebased it; it merges automatically when its CI is green. The build is done and waiting in PR #219 (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/219), which isn't merged or deployed yet.

**PR #219, commit 1: accepting local backups for the beta (ADR-087)**
- **The command:** `cp-manage node backup-accept-local --name node-01 --until <date> --reason <text>` records who accepted, why and until when; `--revoke` withdraws it.
- **Limits:** it refuses a past date, more than 90 days, or no reason. The database enforces the 90-day limit and "all fields or none" itself, so even a direct write can't stretch it.
- **What it changes:** only the "backups on the same disk" failure becomes a warning. Archiving, retention, `pgbackrest check` and the 30-day window still fail as before.
- **Preflight** names the acceptance while it's in force, and fails again **the day it lapses** without waiting for the next backup check.

**PR #219, commit 2: 7d, the control plane's nightly dump**
- **The command:** `cp-manage control-plane backup --dir <dir> --keep-days 14` writes a timestamped dump with owner-only permissions.
- **Pruning:** older dumps are deleted only after a good new dump, and never the last one, so a run of failed nights doesn't wipe the history.
- **Units:** a service and nightly timer that run as the provisioner user and write only `/var/backups/maludb-control-plane`.
- **Preflight** fails in production when no dump is under 26 hours old.
- **Runbook:** DEPLOYMENT now says to copy the KEK and staff key off the host by hand. A dump can't be restored without them.

**Tests:** 12 new, plus updated preflight and unit tests. 204 and 129 passed across the affected suites, and lint is clean.

**Once you approve merging #219, I'll deploy it:**
1. migration 0059 on the control plane;
2. `node backup-accept-local` for node-01 (I'd use 90 days, until 2026-12-16, with the reason "free-tier beta; off-host targets deferred");
3. `node backup-check`, so preflight's "node backups" passes with the acceptance named;
4. install the dump directory and timer on .173 and take the first dump now.

**7e, the restore drill, needs a yes from you first.** The restore command has to run on the node while writing to the control-plane database. On two machines that means temporarily giving the node:
- the provisioner's database login, with a `pg_hba` line admitting it;
- the KEK.

I'd take one free project back to a point in time **beside** its live database, leaving the live one untouched. Then I'd remove the credentials and the `pg_hba` line straight away. Say "merge 219, deploy, and run the drill" to do all three.

```
### What it refuses to do

**It never writes over a live database.** The recovered data lands in a new
database next to the original. There is no code path that destroys a tenant's
data — a stronger property than "asks for confirmation", and it costs only disk.

**It never drops a cluster it did not create.** `pg_dropcluster` on the wrong
name destroys a node and every tenant on it, and a name cannot check itself. So
creation writes a marker into the cluster's *configuration* directory —
pgBackRest rewrites the data directory during a restore, so a marker there would
be gone exactly when it is needed — and nothing is dropped without it. The live
cluster's `data_directory` is read from the node and compared as well.

**It never reports a restore as complete without checking who owns it.** See
below.

### Ownership, and why it gates activation

This is slice 0's sharpest finding and it produces no error at all. Restoring a
tenant into a cluster that has never seen it moves `auth` and `storage` from
their per-tenant service roles to whoever ran the restore — the platform
superuser — while all 164 RLS policies and every row arrive intact and
`pg_restore` exits 1 with "errors ignored".

ADR-059 puts the `storage` schema under a per-tenant role *specifically* so it
is not owned by something with superuser reach, and ADR-061 tells customers they
cannot author policies there on that basis. **A tenant restored the naive way
arrives with a different security posture from the one that was backed up, and
nothing about the database says so.**

So the load refuses outright when the target cluster lacks the tenant's roles —
failing before the load is cheaper than diagnosing after it — and the restore
records whether the schemas came back correctly owned. Activation refuses
without it.

### Activating a restore

```bash
# Stop the project's workers first: a database with open connections
# cannot be renamed.
cp-manage restore activate --ref abcd0001
```

Renames both ways and drops neither. The database that was live is retained as
`mldb_abcd0001_pre_restore_<timestamp>`, so an activation that turns out to have
been the wrong call is reversible with two `ALTER DATABASE ... RENAME TO`.

`cp-manage restore list` shows what has been restored and what became of it.

### Prerequisites and limits

- **Disk is the real constraint, not time.** A scratch restore holds a second
```

def create_scratch_cluster(
    admin_conn: psycopg.Connection,
    *,
    version: str = DEFAULT_PG_VERSION,
    name: str = DEFAULT_SCRATCH_CLUSTER,
    port: int = DEFAULT_SCRATCH_PORT,
    run_as: str = "postgres",
) -> ScratchCluster:
    """Build an empty cluster for one restore to be poured into.

    Refuses to build over the live cluster, and refuses to reuse a cluster it
    did not create. Both are checks on the same mistake from opposite ends: this
    function's next act is to empty a data directory, and the cost of emptying
    the wrong one is every tenant on the node.
    """
    cluster = ScratchCluster(
        version=checked_pg_version(version),
        name=checked_cluster(name),
        port=int(port),
        run_as=backup.checked_run_as(run_as),
    )

    live = _live_data_directory(admin_conn)
    if os.path.normpath(cluster.data_dir) == os.path.normpath(live):
        raise RestoreError(
            f"the scratch cluster's data directory is the live one ({live}); refusing. "
            "A restore never writes over the node it is restoring from"
        )

    if Path(cluster.data_dir).exists() and not cluster.is_ours:
        raise RestoreError(
            f"a cluster already exists at {cluster.data_dir} and carries no MaluDB scratch "
            f"marker ({cluster.marker_path}). Refusing to reuse or destroy it -- if it really "
            "is scrap, remove it by hand"
        )

    drop_scratch_cluster(cluster, missing_ok=True)

    made = _run(
        ["pg_createcluster", cluster.version, cluster.name, "--port", str(cluster.port),
         "--", "--auth-local=peer"],
        sudo=True,
    )
    if made.returncode != 0:
        raise RestoreError(f"pg_createcluster failed: {_tail(made.stderr or made.stdout)}")
def drop_scratch_cluster(cluster: ScratchCluster, *, missing_ok: bool = False) -> None:
    """Destroy a scratch cluster, and only a scratch cluster.

    The marker is the authority. A cluster without one is not dropped, whatever
    its name says — because the only way this function is ever dangerous is if
    the name is wrong, and a name cannot check itself.
    """
    if not Path(cluster.config_dir).exists():
        if missing_ok:
            return
        raise RestoreError(f"no cluster at {cluster.config_dir}")

    if not cluster.is_ours:
        if missing_ok:
            # Reached from `create_scratch_cluster`, which has already refused
            # an unmarked cluster by this point; belt and braces.
            raise RestoreError(
                f"{cluster.config_dir} exists without a MaluDB scratch marker; refusing to drop it"
            )
        raise RestoreError(
            f"{cluster.config_dir} carries no MaluDB scratch marker; refusing to drop it"
        )

    dropped = _run(["pg_dropcluster", "--stop", cluster.version, cluster.name], sudo=True)
    if dropped.returncode != 0:
        raise RestoreError(f"pg_dropcluster failed: {_tail(dropped.stderr or dropped.stdout)}")

## 🤖 Claude

The restore drill passed: a point-in-time restore of project `8zn07rbf` came back exactly as it was at the target time, beside a live database that wasn't touched. #219 is also merged and deployed, and preflight now has no failures.

**Deploy of #219** (with #218 merged too, at 9fa538c on both VMs)
- **Migration 0059** is applied, and node-01's local backups are accepted until **2026-12-16**. It shows the operator as `maludb`, the SSH account.
- **`node backup-check`:** ready. The same-disk repository appears as a warning naming the acceptance.
- **Control-plane dump:** the first one is written (324 KB, key rows present), and the nightly timer is on.
- **Preflight:** exit 2 with no failures. The warnings are the gateway role (can't be checked from this host) and the console config (not read from `provisioner.env`).

**The drill**
- **Setup:** through the SQL console, I created a marker table in `8zn07rbf` with value `before`, noted the time (17:40:30 UTC), then changed it to `after`.
- **Plan check first:** the platform refused a point-in-time restore of a free project, which is correct, because the free plan only promises a restore to the latest backup. For the drill I used the logged operator override `--beyond-entitlement`, since point-in-time also tests the WAL archive.
- **Result, in 39 seconds:**
  - the restored copy said **`before`** and the live database still said **`after`**;
  - `auth` and `storage` came back owned by their per-tenant roles;
  - the other database on the node kept answering throughout.
- **Temporary access, all removed afterwards:**
  - a `pg_hba` line on each VM;
  - a minimal root-only env file on the node, with none of the MaluMail, Turnstile or S3 secrets.
- **Cleanup confirmed:** the env file is shredded, both lines are gone (the node is now refused when it tries the control-plane login), and the restored copy and the marker table are dropped.

**Finding (not fixed yet):** after dropping the scratch cluster, the restore leaves `/etc/postgresql/17/mldbrestore/` behind with its "this is ours" marker file. I removed it by hand. The risk is low, because PostgreSQL won't create a new cluster over an existing config directory, but the marker is the safety guard and shouldn't outlive its cluster. The fix is a few lines in `restore.py`.

**Left in slice 7:**
- **Marker fix:** a small PR.
- **Control-plane dump drill:** restore last night's dump into a scratch database and run `control-plane verify --reach-nodes`. It needs no temporary access, since it runs on the control plane.
- **Your one manual step:** copy `/etc/maludb/keys/kek` and `/etc/maludb/keys/staff-key` off the control plane into your password manager, by hand. A dump is useless without them.

def test_an_unmarked_cluster_is_never_dropped(tmp_path):
    """The guard that stands between this module and a live node.

    A name cannot check itself, so creation writes a marker into the *config*
    directory — pgBackRest rewrites the data directory during a restore, so a
    marker there would be gone at exactly the moment it is needed — and nothing
    is dropped without it.
    """
    cluster = restore.ScratchCluster(
        version="17", name="pretendlive", port=5999, run_as="postgres",
        data_root=str(tmp_path / "data"), config_root=str(tmp_path / "etc"),
    )
    (tmp_path / "etc" / "17" / "pretendlive").mkdir(parents=True)

    assert cluster.is_ours is False
    with pytest.raises(restore.RestoreError, match="no MaluDB scratch marker"):
        restore.drop_scratch_cluster(cluster)


def test_a_marked_cluster_is_recognised_as_ours(tmp_path):
    cluster = restore.ScratchCluster(
        version="17", name="scratch", port=5999, run_as="postgres",
        data_root=str(tmp_path / "data"), config_root=str(tmp_path / "etc"),
    )
    config_dir = tmp_path / "etc" / "17" / "scratch"
    config_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (config_dir / restore.SCRATCH_MARKER).write_text("")
    assert cluster.is_ours is True


def test_dropping_a_cluster_that_does_not_exist_is_not_an_error_when_asked(tmp_path):
    cluster = restore.ScratchCluster(
        version="17", name="absent", port=5999, run_as="postgres",
        data_root=str(tmp_path / "data"), config_root=str(tmp_path / "etc"),
    )
    restore.drop_scratch_cluster(cluster, missing_ok=True)
    with pytest.raises(restore.RestoreError):
        restore.drop_scratch_cluster(cluster)

I fixed the marker bug, and the control-plane dump drill passed. With the earlier node drill, both kinds of backup have now been restored and checked on the real VMs.

**Marker fix: PR #220** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/220), not merged
- **The bug was worse than a leftover file.** The leftover marker would have made the **next** restore fail, because restore tried to drop a cluster that no longer existed.
- **Cleanup after a drop:** once `pg_dropcluster` succeeds, the restore now removes the marker and deletes the config directory only if that leaves it empty. Anything else in there stays for a person to look at.
- **Stale marker:** a directory holding only a marker and no data is now recognised as leftover and cleared, without calling `pg_dropcluster`.
- **Tests:** 3 new; 86 passed across the restore and backup suites, including the real scratch-cluster tests.
- **Plan:** the PR also records the 7d and 7e results.

**Control-plane dump drill (on .173)**
- **Restore:** last night's dump (`cp-20260917T173944Z.sql`) loaded into a scratch database in 3 seconds, with psql told to stop at the first error.
- **Verify:** `control-plane verify --reach-nodes` passed:
  - the KEK unlocked the data key, node-01's admin credential and a sample of 3 of the 8 project credentials;
  - node-01 accepted a connection with the credential recovered from the dump.
- **Cleanup:** the scratch database is dropped. No temporary access was needed.

**Slice 7 status**
- **Node backups:** WAL archiving, a nightly full backup and diffs every 6 hours, kept 30 days. They're local by your decision (ADR-087), accepted until 2026-12-16, and the point-in-time restore is proven.
- **Control plane:** nightly dumps kept 14 days, and restore is proven.
- **Preflight:** no failures.

**Still yours:** copy `/etc/maludb/keys/kek` and `/etc/maludb/keys/staff-key` off the control plane into your password manager, by hand. The drill just showed a dump is only recoverable with the KEK. If the control-plane VM is lost, both are gone together.

Next is slice 8: making the signup and sign-in rate limits see real client IP addresses behind the proxy, and naming an abuse reviewer (H-5).

**Done and verified on test.maludb.org (slices 1–7):** the maintenance pass, email, Auth, Storage, memory spaces, vector search and the schema graph, and backups with both restore drills passed. Preflight has no failures.

**Engineering left**

| Slice | What | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **8: rate limits see real clients** | Signup and sign-in limits currently see every request as coming from the proxy, so one abuser throttles everyone or no one. Decide which proxy hops to trust, set it on the public app and the gateway, and prove the limits count per address. Turnstile is already done. | Small–medium |
| **9: public site says what's true** | Pricing shows Developer as available and paid tiers as "coming"; links to terms, privacy, AUP and support; check every docs claim against what we verified (for example, free projects get restore-to-latest-backup, not point-in-time); a decision on the missing console controls for graph and vectors (add buttons, or document the API route). `MALUDB_SIGNUPS_OPEN = true` is the very last change. | Medium; most of it waits on your text |
| **10: leftovers and the launch check** | Remove the old install's services, disabled but still present on both VMs (`maludb-api`, `maludb-mc2dbd`, `maludb-modeld`); remove or explain the `10.120.0.250` `pg_hba` line on each VM; decide finding 11 (a startup race on the first data key); complete DEPLOYMENT §5; then the real test: a stranger signs up on the live site and every feature works from the official client. | Medium |

**Yours** (these block launch more than the code does)
- **H-4:** terms of service, privacy policy and acceptable-use text.
- **H-5:** who reviews the abuse report, and how often.
- **H-6:** a support address, and where incidents get announced.

**Risks to accept explicitly for the beta** (I'll record them in the plan's decision log)

"""Rate-limit dependencies for the routes an anonymous caller can reach.

Deliberately shaped like `auth_dep`: a dependency rather than middleware, so a
route that should be limited says so in its own signature and a reviewer can see
which routes are protected by reading them rather than by reading a table of
path prefixes somewhere else.

The limiter itself is `services.control_plane.ratelimit`, one instance per
application, held on `app.state` so a test can drive it with its own clock.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import HTTPException, Request, status

from services.control_plane import ratelimit


def client_key(request: Request) -> str:
    """Who this call is counted against.

    The peer address by default. `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured **only** when the
    deployment says a proxy it controls rewrites it (`trust_forwarded_for`),
    because a forwarded header that nothing strips is attacker-controlled: a
    caller that can set it picks its own bucket, and every limit built on it
    counts one attempt each for a million invented clients.

    When trusted, the *last* hop is used rather than the first. The first entry
    is whatever the original client claimed; the last is what the proxy nearest
    this service observed, and only the latter is a fact.
    """
    config = request.app.state.config
    if config.trust_forwarded_for:
        forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for", "")
        hops = [hop.strip() for hop in forwarded.split(",") if hop.strip()]
        if hops:
            return hops[-1]
    client = request.client
    # No peer address at all (an ASGI transport that does not report one) counts
    # as a single shared bucket rather than as unlimited. Sharing one bucket is
    # a bad experience for those callers; having none is no limit at all.
    return client.host if client and client.host else "unknown"


def enforce(request: Request, *, bucket: str, limit: ratelimit.Limit, subject: str = "") -> None:
    """Spend one attempt, or raise 429.

    `subject` scopes the bucket to something other than the caller -- an email
    address, for the account half of the signin limit. It is never returned in
    the response, and the refusal is identical whether or not the account
    exists: a 429 that only appeared for real accounts would be an oracle for
    which addresses are registered, which is exactly what the uniform 401 on the
    route below exists to avoid.
    """
    limiter: ratelimit.LocalLimiter = request.app.state.limiter
    key = f"{bucket}:{subject or client_key(request)}"
    decision = limiter.check(key, limit)
    if decision.allowed:
        return
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
        detail="too many attempts; try again later",
        headers={"Retry-After": str(decision.retry_after_seconds)},
    )

# -- who a call is counted against ----------------------------------------


class _Request:
    """The two attributes `client_key` reads, without an ASGI server."""

    def __init__(self, config, *, host: str | None, forwarded: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.app = type("app", (), {"state": type("state", (), {"config": config})})
        self.headers = {"x-forwarded-for": forwarded} if forwarded else {}
        self.client = type("client", (), {"host": host}) if host else None


def test_a_forwarded_header_is_ignored_unless_the_deployment_trusts_it(app_config):
    """Trusting it by default would let every caller pick its own bucket.

    Which is not a weaker limit but no limit: a caller that chooses the key its
    attempts are counted against can present a new one per attempt.
    """
    untrusting = dataclasses.replace(app_config, trust_forwarded_for=False)
    request = _Request(untrusting, host="10.0.0.9", forwarded="1.2.3.4")
    assert limit_dep.client_key(request) == "10.0.0.9"


def test_a_trusted_deployment_reads_the_last_hop(app_config):
    """The first entry is what the client claimed; the last is what we observed."""
    trusting = dataclasses.replace(app_config, trust_forwarded_for=True)
    request = _Request(trusting, host="10.0.0.9", forwarded="1.2.3.4, 203.0.113.7")
    assert limit_dep.client_key(request) == "203.0.113.7"


def test_a_call_with_no_peer_address_shares_one_bucket_rather_than_none(app_config):
    request = _Request(app_config, host=None)
    assert limit_dep.client_key(request) == "unknown"

## 3. The website

Five static files. `dev-server.py` is a development proxy and is **not**
deployed.

```
frontend/index.html  frontend/app.js  frontend/api.js  frontend/styles.css  frontend/docs.html
```

**Do not put the repository inside the document root.** Apache will serve
`/.git/config`, and the whole history is reconstructable from there. Clone
above the docroot and point at the subdirectory:

```apache
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName example.com
    DocumentRoot /opt/maludb/frontend

    <Directory /opt/maludb/frontend>
        Require all granted
        AllowOverride None
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
    </Directory>

    <FilesMatch "\.(py|md)$">
        Require all denied
    </FilesMatch>

    # ES modules are refused otherwise. (Apache has no trailing comments: on the
    # directive's own line these words would be read as more extensions.)
    AddType text/javascript .js

    # Required once signups open. See below.
    ProxyPass        /api/ http://127.0.0.1:8112/
    ProxyPassReverse /api/ http://127.0.0.1:8112/
</VirtualHost>
```

`a2enmod proxy proxy_http` first. **Behind a TLS proxy on another host** (Nginx
Proxy Manager, a load balancer) the same block listens on `*:80` for that proxy
alone. Know what that costs before opening signups: the public app then sees
every request from 127.0.0.1, with the proxy's address as the last
`X-Forwarded-For` hop, so signup and sign-in rate limits cannot tell customers
apart. Not yet solved (`plans/active/deployment-rehearsal.md`, finding 19).

### The same-origin constraint

**There is no CORS middleware in the control plane.** The page and the API must
therefore share an origin:

| Works | Does not |
|---|---|
| `example.com` and `example.com/api/*` | `www.example.com` and `api.example.com` |

Split hostnames fail every browser call on CORS preflight, and it presents as a
broken frontend rather than a missing header. Decide before issuing certificates.

While signups are closed the page makes **no API calls at all** — pricing is
rendered from a bundled copy — so the site can be published before the control
plane exists.

## 🤖 Claude

Here's where things stand.

**How much is left for the free tier:** engineering is about three-quarters done. Slices 1–7 are built, deployed and verified on test.maludb.org. What remains is slice 8 (in progress), slice 9 (mostly your text), and slice 10 (cleanup plus a real signup walkthrough) — roughly 2–3 more sessions like today. The bigger dependency is you: terms/privacy/AUP (H-4), an abuse reviewer (H-5), a support address (H-6), and copying the KEK off the host.

**#220** (the scratch-marker fix) is still in CI. Its watcher merges it automatically when green.

**Slice 8 started, and the bug is confirmed on the real deployment.** The chain is visitor → Nginx Proxy Manager (TLS) → Apache → uvicorn, so:
- Apache put **NPM's** address in the last `X-Forwarded-For` hop, and the code trusted the last hop;
- uvicorn also rewrote the client address on its own, because Apache connects from loopback;
- so every visitor was recorded as `10.120.0.1`. Signup and sign-in limits treated the entire internet as one client, and sessions and audit rows logged the proxy as everyone's address.

**The fix is in PR #221** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/221), not merged:
- **`MALUDB_TRUSTED_PROXIES`** names the proxies in front. The client is the rightmost forwarded address that isn't one of them. Anything a caller forges sits to the left of what a proxy actually observed, so it can never be picked.
- **A range covering the internet is refused** outright, since trusting everyone would let each caller choose its own bucket.
- **`--no-proxy-headers`** on the three control-plane units stops uvicorn substituting its own guess.
- **Sessions, audit rows and the captcha check** now use the same address as the limits.
- **Tests:** 232 passed, including the two-proxy topology, forged headers, direct connections that bypass the proxies, and the config refusals.

**To finish slice 8 I need you to merge #221 so I can deploy it.** Then I'll set `MALUDB_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,10.120.0.1` on .173 and prove it from outside: two different clients get separate buckets, and a forged header can't move one caller into another's.

The other half of slice 8 is **H-5**: who reviews the abuse report, and how often.

@router.post("/signin", response_model=SessionOut, summary="Exchange credentials for a session")
def signin(body: SigninIn, request: Request) -> SessionOut:
    # Two limits, counting two different things. Per source bounds attempts and
    # is released on success; per account bounds *failures*, which is what a
    # distributed credential-stuffing run produces and what a legitimate user
    # does not.
    email = str(body.email).strip().lower()
    account_limit = limit_dep.signin_account_limit(request)
    limit_dep.enforce(request, bucket="signin", limit=limit_dep.signin_limit(request))
    limit_dep.guard(request, bucket="signin-account", limit=account_limit, subject=email)
    with db.connection() as conn:
        user = identity.authenticate(conn, email=str(body.email), password=body.password)
        if user is None:
            # Charged on failure only. An account bucket spent per *attempt*
            # would ration the person it protects -- several devices, or a
            # session lifetime short enough to sign in daily, and they exhaust
            # their own allowance by using the platform correctly.
            limit_dep.spend(request, bucket="signin-account", limit=account_limit, subject=email)
            # One message for both unknown account and wrong password.
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
                detail="invalid email or password",
            )

## 🤖 Claude

**The fix works.** Same test, after deploy:

| Client | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Dev box, 22 attempts | 20 × 401 then 429 | 20 × 401 then 429 (unchanged, correct) |
| Dev box with forged `X-Forwarded-For` | — | **429**: it can't claim a fresh bucket |
| Node .172 (different client) | **429** on its first attempt | **401**: its own bucket |
| Control plane .173 (third client) | — | **401**: its own bucket |

So the limits now count per visitor, a forged header can't move a caller out of its bucket, and one abuser no longer locks out everyone else. Recording the result and closing finding 19 in the plans.

Here's exactly what I need, and what I'll do with each.

**Slice 8 — one item (H-5)**

**Who reviews the abuse report, and how often.** The report already exists in two places: `cp-manage abuse report` and the operator console's "Abuse review" page. It lists free projects sitting near their limits. What's missing is a named person and a cadence, so it isn't just a page nobody opens.
- **What I need:** a name or role, and an interval (weekly is the usual choice for a beta).
- **What I'll do:** record it in the launch plan and DEPLOYMENT §5, and add a line to the console page saying who owns it and when it was last reviewed.
- **If you'd rather not decide now:** I can write "the owner, weekly" and you can change it later.

**Slice 9 — four items**

1. **Legal text (H-4): terms of service, privacy policy, acceptable use.** The site has no links today.
   - **What I need:** the text, or a decision to link to something you host elsewhere.
   - **Warning:** I can draft plain-English starting points, but I'm not a lawyer and this is a real service taking people's data. Treat anything I write as a draft for review.
   - **Minimum for a beta:** what the service is, that it's a beta with no uptime promise, that backups are local and a host loss can lose data, what data you store, and how someone deletes their account.
2. **Support address and incident channel (H-6).** The site currently shows `hello@maludb.com` as a waitlist address.
   - **What I need:** the address customers should use, and where you'll announce incidents (a status page, a mailing list, or "email only").

   - **What I need:** either "add the buttons" (a few hours of frontend work) or "document the API route" for the beta.
   - **My recommendation:** add the buttons. It's the one feature a customer can't reach from the console.
4. **The beta's honest limits.** I'll write the pricing and docs copy, but you should confirm the wording:
   - one node, and signups close when it fills;
   - backups are local until 2026-12-16 (ADR-087), so losing the host loses data;
   - customer files have a single copy;
   - free projects get restore to the latest backup, not point-in-time.

**Not blocking:** slice 10 needs nothing from you, so I can start it whenever you like.
