/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Memory spaces (ADR-079)
 *
 * The control-plane half of memory: spaces, their models, and the project's
 * provider keys. Ingest and search run on the project's own host with its
 * secret key, not here -- a person's session never writes a memory.
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/** The project's spaces and its plan's memory limits. Members may read it. */
export const listMemorySpaces = (ref) => api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/spaces`);

/** Owner or admin. 202 while it is built; 200 when it already exists. */
export const createMemorySpace = (ref, name) =>
  api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/spaces`, { method: "POST", body: { name } });

/** Owner or admin. Irreversible: the space and every memory in it are removed. */
export const deleteMemorySpace = (ref, name) =>
  api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/spaces/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { method: "DELETE" });

/** Owner or admin. Model names may be empty, which means the provider's default. */
export const setMemoryModels = (ref, name, models) =>
  api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/spaces/${encodeURIComponent(name)}/models`, { method: "PUT", body: models });

/** Which providers have a key set, and each key's last four characters. Never a key. */
export const listProviderKeys = (ref) => api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/provider-keys`);

/** Owner or admin. Write-only: no route returns the key afterwards. */
export const setProviderKey = (ref, provider, apiKey) =>
  api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/provider-keys/${encodeURIComponent(provider)}`, {
    method: "PUT",
    body: { api_key: apiKey },
  });

export const removeProviderKey = (ref, provider) =>
  api(`${projectPath(ref)}/maludb/memory/provider-keys/${encodeURIComponent(provider)}`, { method: "DELETE" });

        <section id="memory">
          <h2>Memory spaces</h2>
          <p>Long-term memory for your agents: send what they learned as text, and search it later by meaning, narrowed to a
            subject or a verb. A project can hold several named spaces; nothing is shared between them.
            <strong>Server-side only</strong> — every memory call takes the <strong>secret key</strong>.</p>

          <h3>Set it up in the dashboard</h3>
          <ol class="steps">
            <li>On a ready project, open <strong>Memory</strong> and <strong>create a space</strong> (lower-case letters, digits,
              underscores, e.g. <code>support_bot</code>).</li>
            <li><strong>Set provider keys</strong> — your own accounts do the model work, and bill you for it:
              an <strong>Anthropic</strong> or <strong>OpenAI</strong> key to find the statements in a text, and an
              <strong>OpenAI</strong> or <strong>Voyage</strong> key to embed them. (Anthropic has no embeddings; Anthropic
              recommends Voyage.) Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.</li>
            <li>Under the space's <strong>Models</strong>, choose the providers. The defaults are sensible; pick another
              model from the list, or <em>Other model…</em> for one that is not listed.</li>
          </ol>
          <p><strong>The embedding model is fixed once a space holds memories</strong> — search compares only vectors from one
            model. To change it, create a new space.</p>

          <h3>Store memories</h3>
<pre><code>curl -X POST &lt;project URL&gt;/memory/v1/spaces/support_bot/ingest \
  -H 'apikey: &lt;secret key&gt;' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items": [{"title": "parser ownership",
                  "text": "Carol owns the parser module and reviews every change to it."}]}'</code></pre>
          <p>The answer is <code>202</code> with an <code>id</code> and a <code>status_url</code>; the work happens in the
            background, usually within seconds:</p>
<pre><code>curl &lt;project URL&gt;/memory/v1/ingests/&lt;id&gt; -H 'apikey: &lt;secret key&gt;'
# {"state": "succeeded", "items": 1, "written": 1, "results": [{"edges": [{"subject": "Carol", "verb": "owns", …}]}]}</code></pre>

          <h3>Search</h3>
<pre><code>curl -X POST &lt;project URL&gt;/memory/v1/spaces/support_bot/search \
  -H 'apikey: &lt;secret key&gt;' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "who is responsible for the parser?", "subject": "Carol", "limit": 5}'
# [{"content": "Carol owns the parser module", "similarity": 0.83, "subject_name": "Carol", …}]</code></pre>
          <p>A search names a <code>subject</code> or a <code>verb</code> (or both). If you compute embeddings yourself, store
            items with an <code>embedding</code> instead of <code>text</code> and search with a vector through the client —
            no provider key needed:</p>
<pre><code>await supabase.schema('maludb').rpc('memory_search', { space: 'support_bot', query: [0.1, 0.2, …], subject: 'Carol' })</code></pre>
          <p>If a provider refuses — a wrong key, or its rate limit on a new account — the ingest or search reports the
            provider's own message, so you know which account to look at.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- ------------------------------------------------------------ -->
        <section id="not-yet">
          <h2>Not yet available</h2>

  const plan = params.get("plan") || "free";
  const min = params.get("min_percent") || "50";
  const rows = await api(`/abuse?plan=${encodeURIComponent(plan)}&min_percent=${encodeURIComponent(min)}`);
  return `

    ${tableCard("Pressure", USAGE_HEAD, usageRows(rows), "Nothing at or above that pressure.")}`;
}

async function nodesPage() {
  const nodes = await api("/nodes");
  if (!nodes.length) return `<div class="card"><p class="usage-note">No nodes registered.</p></div>`;
  const meter = (used, limit) => {
    const pct = limit > 0 ? Math.min(100, Math.round((Number(used) / Number(limit)) * 100)) : 100;
    return `<div class="mini-meter"><small>${count(used)} / ${count(limit)}</small>
      <div class="usage-bar"><span data-pct="${Number(pct)}"></span></div></div>`;
  };

**PR #223 — console buttons and the abuse cadence** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/223)
- **A MaluDB page on every project.** For the schema graph and vector compartments it shows whether each is on, the plan's limits, and the latest job, with buttons to turn them on or off (plus **Refresh now** for the graph). That closes the gap you hit in slice 6, where a personal access token was the only way in.
- **It follows the work.** Enabling is queued and runs on the project's host, so the page tracks the job rather than guessing.
- **It offers no reader**, because both features are read with the project's **secret key**, which a browser session isn't. The page shows an example instead.
- **Only owners and admins** see the buttons, matching the API.
- **Docs:** `docs.html` gains the section the page links to; there was nothing on either feature before.
- **H-5 recorded:** the console's Abuse review page and DEPLOYMENT §5 both state that **the owner reviews it weekly**.
- I rendered the page to check the layout. 78 tests pass.

**PR #224 — legal drafts** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/224)
- **Terms, Privacy and Acceptable Use**, written from what the platform actually does, linked from both footers and from the signup form.
- **They state the beta's real limits** rather than a template's promises: one machine, backups kept beside the data, a single copy of uploaded files, and restore to the most recent backup for free projects.
- **Privacy lists only the processors the code calls** (MaluMail, Cloudflare Turnstile, the host), and says memory providers are called with *your customers' own keys*, under their own agreements.
- **Acceptable use** describes enforcement as it works: automatic limits, the weekly report, and suspension as a human decision.
- **Tests** hold those claims and keep every operator blank visible as a `[PLACEHOLDER]`.

2. **It won't launch as-is.** Every `[PLACEHOLDER]` needs filling: legal entity, registered address, jurisdiction, retention periods, the liability amount, and the support, security and abuse addresses (H-6).

## 🤖 Claude

Fix for finding 11: take a transaction-scoped advisory lock before checking for keys, re-read inside it, and make the insert conflict-proof. The loser then reads the winner's key instead of crashing. Implementing, with a test that runs two real listeners' key loads concurrently against a scratch database.

## 🤖 Claude

Two real findings from my own tests:
1. The lock outlived its transaction, because `load()` already had one open, so my nested block became a savepoint. Making the commit explicit, as the old code did, releases it deterministically.
2. My test row violated a `nodes` constraint. Checking which table to use for the "ciphertext but no keys" case.

## 5. Before announcing

Start with the command, then do the things it cannot see:

```bash
cp-manage deploy preflight
```

Exit 0 is clean, 1 has failures, 2 is ready with advisories worth reading. It
checks the plan catalogue, the gateway domain, node placeability and backup
stanzas, the ADR-072 gateway role, and billing. It **cannot** prove the internal
listener is unreachable, that DNS resolves, or that a certificate is valid --
those are properties of the network, and the list below is how they get checked.


- [ ] `curl https://<internal-host>:8111/healthz` from **outside** the private
      network fails to connect. This is the ADR-037 property and the only way to
      confirm it is from outside the machine.
- [ ] `cp-manage plans list` shows the plans you intend to sell.
- [ ] `cp-manage node list` shows the node active with fresh health.
- [ ] `cp-manage gateway grant --role gw --node <node>` exits 0, reports the
      admin columns unreadable, and names the node whose projects are the only
      rows that role can see.
- [ ] `cp-manage billing status` reports the deployment can take money, if it
      should.
- [ ] A real signup through the real site reaches a project that becomes ACTIVE.
- [ ] `cp-manage control-plane backup --path /var/backups/cp.dump` runs, and
      its output is stored somewhere that is not the control-plane host.
      Store the KEK separately: ADR-070 makes a dump without its keys not a
      backup, and the control plane refuses to start rather than mint new ones.

## 🤖 Claude

Slice 10 is underway. #223 is merged; #224 merges when its CI finishes.

**Done**
- **Finding 11 fixed — PR #225** (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/225), the last open finding from the rehearsal. Two listeners starting together both minted the first encryption key and one crashed. Now the check and insert happen under a lock, and the second listener picks up the first one's key. The guard that refuses to mint a key over a restored database is untouched and now has its own test. The tests run a real race against a scratch database; 70 tests pass.
- **Old install removed from both VMs.** The three disabled units (`maludb-api`, `maludb-mc2dbd`, `maludb-modeld`) are gone, with copies kept in `/root/removed-units-2026-09-17` in case you want them. Every service still runs, nothing failed, the site returns 200 and the project API still answers.
- **DEPLOYMENT §5 rewritten** around what the deployment actually has now: the node's backups and their recorded acceptance, **a restore that has been run rather than recorded**, the trusted-proxy setting, the abuse cadence, the legal pages, no leftovers from a previous install, and signups opened last.

**One thing I won't touch without you**

Both VMs carry this line in `pg_hba.conf`:

```
host all all 10.120.0.250/32 scram-sha-256
```

That's **any role, into any database, with TLS not required**, from 10.120.0.250. That host answers ping, but nothing in the repo or the runbook names it, and it isn't this dev box (which is .165). It's left over from the previous install.

**What is 10.120.0.250?** Then I'll either remove the line, or narrow it to a named role over TLS and document why it exists.

**Left after that:** deploy #223–#225, your legal placeholders and a lawyer's read (H-4), the support/security/abuse addresses (H-6), the signup walkthrough, and finally turning signups on.

## 🤖 Claude

The walkthrough worked, and it found one launch blocker.

**What passed**, as a stranger would do it:
- **The real form:** the page, legal links and footer render, and **Turnstile refused to submit without a solved challenge**. Cloudflare blocked my automated browser, which is the widget doing its job — so a human still needs to do one browser signup by hand.
- **The rest, through the API** with the challenge briefly disabled: signup (201), sign-in, a personal organization, and a project that reached PROVISIONED (serving).
- **The project works:** publishable and secret keys issued, a table created through the SQL editor, and with the official Supabase client the secret key reads and writes, project Auth accepts a signup, and Storage creates a bucket, uploads and downloads.
- **Restored afterwards:** the challenge is required again, signups are closed again, and an unchallenged signup is refused (400). I revoked the walkthrough keys.

**Expected, not a fault:** a new table has no row-level security, so the publishable key can read it — same as Supabase. The docs say to turn RLS on, and the table browser warns about that exact table. My test asserted the wrong thing.

**The blocker: nothing can delete a project.** There's no customer route, no `cp-manage` command, and `project cleanup` refuses any database that was ever provisioned. That matters three ways:
1. **The legal pages I drafted promise deletion** ("delete a project or your account at any time", and deletion on request in Privacy). Today that's untrue.
2. **A beta stores personal data**, so honouring a deletion request needs to be possible.
3. **Right now it's visible:** the walkthrough's project `3u2rzs6e` and its account can't be removed, and they hold a project slot on the node.

I've written it up as **slice 10b**. Most of the machinery exists — `jobs.cleanup` already drops roles, the database and the project's objects for failed projects — so the work is a guarded path for a live project: a customer route that marks it and queues the work, an operator command, the storage tenant deregistered, keys revoked, and the record kept.

**Also worth noting:** provisioning took **208 seconds**, where the docs and console copy say "about a minute". Either the copy or the timing should change.

**Your call:** shall I build slice 10b now? The alternative is to change the Terms and Privacy pages to promise deletion by request, which I'd rather not do while nobody can actually perform it.

def cleanup(
    conn: psycopg.Connection,
    admin_conn: psycopg.Connection,
    *,
    project_id: uuid.UUID,
    tenant_connect: Callable[[str], psycopg.Connection],
    allow_database_drop: bool = False,
    config: Any | None = None,
) -> CleanupReport:
    """Reclaim what a failed provisioning run left behind.

    The invariant from `specs/provisioning-state-machine.md`: once a project may
    contain customer data, cleanup must never drop the database merely to
    restore desired state. So this drops nothing by default, and even when told
    it may, it still refuses if the database was ever handed over or holds a
    single object the tenant created.

    Roles are only removed once the database is gone. Dropping them first would
    leave a database whose grants name roles that no longer exist and whose
    owner may have vanished — reachable by nobody, reclaimable by nothing.
    """
    project = db.one(
        conn,
        "SELECT project_ref, status, database_name, provisioned_at FROM projects WHERE id = %s",
        (project_id,),
    )
    if project is None:
        raise ProvisioningError("project does not exist")

    # Explicit state check, per AGENTS.md. A PROVISIONED or ACTIVE project is
    # not a cleanup candidate at any privilege level; deletion is its own path.
    if project["status"] not in CLEANABLE_STATES:
        raise ProvisioningError(
            f"refusing to clean up a project in {project['status']}; "
            f"cleanup handles {' and '.join(CLEANABLE_STATES)} only"
        )

    # A retry worker may be mid-flight on this project right now. Cleanup would
    # drop the database out from under it, and the run would carry on against
    # something that no longer exists.
    open_job = db.one(
        conn,
        "SELECT attempt, state FROM provisioning_jobs WHERE project_id = %s AND completed_at IS NULL",
        (project_id,),
    )
    if open_job is not None:
        raise ProvisioningError(
            f"a provisioning run is in progress for this project (attempt {open_job['attempt']}, "
            f"{open_job['state']}); wait for it to finish or fail before cleaning up"
        )

    names = TenantNames.for_ref(project["project_ref"])
    database = project["database_name"]

    # Defence in depth on the one operation here that destroys data. The name is
    # composed with sql.Identifier so this is not an injection concern -- it is
    # that a database_name which disagrees with the project's own ref means
    # dropping some other tenant's database. Nothing should ever write one, so
    # finding one is a reason to stop rather than to proceed carefully.
```

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Claim:
    project_id: uuid.UUID
    project_ref: str
    node_id: int


def claim_one(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> Claim | None:
    """Take the project that has waited longest, or return None.

    `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is what makes a second worker safe. The row stays
    locked for the life of the caller's transaction, so the caller commits
    before doing any node work -- holding a control-plane transaction open for
    the nine seconds a bootstrap takes would be a lock on the project row for
    every reader of it, including the customer polling for status.
    """
    row = db.one(
        conn,
        """
        SELECT id, project_ref, node_id
          FROM projects
         WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
           AND node_id IS NOT NULL
           AND status = ANY(%s)
           AND (retry_after IS NULL OR retry_after <= now())
           AND provisioning_failures < %s
         ORDER BY requested_at NULLS FIRST, created_at
         FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
         LIMIT 1
        """,
        (list(CLAIMABLE_STATUSES), jobs.MAX_ATTEMPTS),
    )
    if row is None:
        return None
    return Claim(project_id=row["id"], project_ref=row["project_ref"], node_id=row["node_id"])


def provision_claim(claim: Claim, *, key_ring: crypto.KeyRing, platform_owner: str) -> bool:
    """Do the node work for one claimed project. True if it reached ACTIVE.

    The node's admin credential is decrypted here, handed straight to psycopg
    and never logged -- the same handling `cp-manage` uses, in the process ADR
    -038 says is allowed to have it.
    """
    with db.connection() as conn:
        dsn = nodes.admin_dsn(conn, node_id=claim.node_id, key_ring=key_ring)

    def tenant_connect(database: str):
        parsed = psycopg.conninfo.conninfo_to_dict(dsn)
        parsed["dbname"] = database
    """Claim and provision one project. False when there was nothing to do."""
    with db.connection() as conn:
        claim = claim_one(conn)
        # Committed before the node work starts, releasing the row lock. The
        # project's own status is what stops a second worker picking it up:
        # `jobs.provision` moves it out of the claimable statuses as its first
        # act, and `provisioning_jobs_one_open_per_project` refuses a second
        # open attempt even if two workers raced the gap.
        conn.commit()
    if claim is None:
        return False
    provision_claim(claim, key_ring=key_ring, platform_owner=platform_owner)
    return True


def run_maludb_once(*, key_ring: crypto.KeyRing) -> bool:
    """Claim and do one MaluDB data-model request. False when there was nothing to do.

    Phase 12 slice 4 (ADR-074), and vector compartments since compartments slice 2b
    (ADR-077). Here rather than in the public application
    because both kinds run as the node superuser (ADR-038).

    **What reaches the customer is chosen here.** A job's `detail` is shown by
    the status route, so a `MaludbError` -- the platform's own refusal, written to
    be read by a customer, like a squatted schema name -- is passed through, and
    anything else becomes a generic sentence. The exception's own text has come
    from a node and is the one thing that could carry an internal detail to a
    customer, the same reason `provision_claim` keeps it out of the log.
    """
    with db.connection() as conn:
        job = maludb_jobs.claim(conn)
        # Committed before the node work, as `run_once` does: the job is marked
        # running, which is what keeps a second worker off it.
        conn.commit()
    if job is None:
        return False

    try:
        with db.connection() as conn:
            dsn = nodes.admin_dsn(conn, node_id=job["node_id"], key_ring=key_ring)

        def tenant_connect(database: str):
            parsed = psycopg.conninfo.conninfo_to_dict(dsn)
            parsed["dbname"] = database
            return psycopg.connect(psycopg.conninfo.make_conninfo(**parsed), autocommit=T

## 🤖 Claude

Design for 10b, reusing the existing machinery rather than a second destroy path:
1. **Migration:** add `DELETING`/`DELETED` statuses and a `delete_requested_at` column.
2. **`jobs.delete_project`:** deregisters the storage tenant, removes objects, drops the database and roles, revokes keys, then records the project as deleted (row kept, as the audit trail).
3. **Provisioner:** claims projects in `DELETING` and runs the work, like it does provisioning.
4. **Customer route** `DELETE /v1/projects/{ref}` (owner/admin) and an operator command with an explicit confirmation.
5. **Console:** a delete control that makes you type the ref.

def main() -> int:
    cfg = config_module.load()
    cp_logging.configure()
    platform_owner = os.environ.get("MALUDB_PLATFORM_OWNER", "").strip()
    if not platform_owner:
        # Fail closed rather than guess. Owning a tenant database is what makes
        # the platform able to take it back; a wrong owner produces databases
        # nobody can administer.
        log.error("MALUDB_PLATFORM_OWNER is required for the provisioner")
        return 2

    db.init_pool(cfg.database_url)
    key_ring = crypto.KeyRing(cfg.kek)
    with db.connection() as conn:
        key_ring.load(conn)

    stopping = False

    def stop(signum, _frame) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001 - signal handler signature
        nonlocal stopping
        stopping = True
        log.info("provisioner stopping on signal %s", signum)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)

    log.info(
        "provisioner started",
        extra={"extra_fields": {"database": cfg.safe_database_dsn}},
    )
    try:
        while not stopping:
            # A project at a time, and the loop asks again immediately when it
            # found one: a queue that emptied slowly would leave the last
            # customer of a busy minute waiting for a poll interval that exists
            # for the idle case.
            # Alternated rather than drained one after the other, so a burst of
            # project creations cannot starve a customer's refresh, or the
            # reverse.
            provisioned = run_once(key_ring=key_ring, platform_owner=platform_owner)
            requested = run_maludb_once(key_ring=key_ring)
            if not provisioned and not requested:
                time.sleep(IDLE_SLEEP_SECONDS)
    finally:
        db.close_pool()

@router.get("/projects/{project_ref}", response_model=ProjectOut, summary="Get a project by reference")
def get_project(
    project_ref: str, request: Request, principal: CurrentPrincipal
) -> ProjectOut:
    domain = request.app.state.config.gateway_domain
    # Treat the ref as untrusted input; reject malformed values before lookup.
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="project not found")
    with db.connection() as conn:
        project = models.get_project_by_ref(conn, project_ref)

    # Not-a-member and does-not-exist are the same answer. Project refs appear
    # in public hostnames (ADR-008), so a distinguishable response would let
    # anyone confirm which refs are real.
    if project is None or not principal.is_member_of(project.org_id):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="project not found")
    return _to_out(project, gateway_domain=domain)

/** The publishable key, which the API lists with its value. Never a secret: none is listed. */
function overviewKey(project) {
  const listing = state.apiKeys[project.project_ref];
  if (!listing) return `<p class="usage-note">Loading keys…</p>`;
  if (listing.error) return `<p class="form-error">${escapeHtml(listing.error)}</p>`;
  const publishable = listing.find((k) => !k.revoked_at && k.key_type === "publishable" && k.key);

def _function(name: str) -> str:
    section = _section()
    start = section.index(f"function {name}(")
    following = re.search(r"\n(?:async )?function |\n/\* --|\Z", section[start + 1:])

## 🤖 Claude

Good catch by the test suite: importing `jobs` into the public API breaks ADR-038's import-graph guard, because `jobs` is node-side machinery. The request half touches only the control-plane database, so it belongs in `models`, with the destructive half staying in `jobs`.

<details><summary>🔧 Bash</summary>

```json

  "command": "cd /home/maludb/mpa-10b && python3 - <<'PYEOF'\np='services/control_plane/jobs.py'; s=open(p).read()\na=s.index('''def request_deletion(''')\nb=s.index('''def delete_project(''')\nblock=s[a:b]\ns=s[:a]+s[b:]\ns=s.replace('''# What a project may be deleted from. A project still being provisioned is stopped by its own\n# status moving to DELETING; the worker refuses one that is mid-attempt, as cleanup does.\nDELETABLE_STATES = (\n    \"REQUESTED\", \"PLACEMENT_RESERVED\", \"PROVISIONED\", \"ACTIVE\", \"PAUSED\", \"SUSPENDED\",\n    \"FAILED\", \"RETRY_WAIT\",\n)\n\n\n''','''')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\n\np='services/control_plane/models.py'; s=open(p).read()\nhead = '''# -- deleting a project (free slice 10b) -----------------------------------\n#\n# The *request* lives here rather than in `jobs`, and that placement is ADR-038: the public\n# application may not import node-side machinery, and `tests/test_control_plane_surfaces.py`\n# enforces it. Marking a project and revoking its keys is control-plane work -- a status and some\n# rows -- while destroying the tenant is the node superuser's, in the provisioner.\n\n\nclass DeletionRefused(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"The project cannot be marked for deletion; the message is written to be read by a customer.\"\"\"\n\n\n# What a project may be deleted from. It becomes deletable when it settles.\nDELETABLE_STATES = (\n    \"REQUESTED\", \"PLACEMENT_RESERVED\", \"PROVISIONED\", \"ACTIVE\", \"PAUSED\", \"SUSPENDED\",\n    \"FAILED\", \"RETRY_WAIT\",\n)\n\n\n'''\nblock = block.replace(\"raise ProvisioningError(\", \"raise DeletionRefused(\")\ns = s.rstrip(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\\n\\n\" + head + block.rstrip(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\"\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nPYEOF\ngrep -n \"^import\\|^from\" services/control_plane/models.py | head -8; grep -n \"def request_deletion\" services/control_plane/models.py | head -2; .venv/bin/ruff check services 2>&1 | grep -E \"^[A-Z][0-9]+|-->\" | head -6",

## 🤖 Claude

Slice 10b is built and in PR #226 (https://github.com/Mestopholis/maludb-provisioner-api/pull/226), rebased and mergeable. It merges automatically when CI is green, and I'll deploy it after that.

**What it does**
- **Asking to delete answers immediately:** the project stops serving and **every API key is revoked**, so a key already in someone's app stops working at once rather than whenever a worker gets to it.
- **The destruction runs on the node** in the provisioner: the storage registration, the database, the files in the bucket, then the per-tenant roles. That's the same order `cleanup` uses, for the same reasons.
- **The record survives.** The row stays with `deleted_at` set, so the project reference is never handed out again and the audit trail outlives the data.
- **Three ways in:** the API (owner or admin; a stranger gets a 404 so project existence isn't confirmed), `cp-manage project delete` which makes you name the project twice, and a console card that makes you type the reference.
- **Guards:** it refuses anything without a recorded request, a database whose name doesn't match the project's reference, and a project with provisioning still in flight.

**One thing the tests caught:** my first version imported node-side machinery into the public API, which breaks ADR-038. The request half now lives in `models` and only the destructive half is in `jobs`.

**Also handled**
- **#222** — you were right, it never merged and had conflicts in both plan files. Rebased, resolved keeping every true entry, merging when green.
- **#225** merged and deployed to both VMs: the first-key race fix and the rewritten DEPLOYMENT §5.

**Still needed from you before signups open**
1. Fill the legal placeholders and have a lawyer read them (H-4), plus the support, security and abuse addresses (H-6).
2. One browser signup by hand, since Cloudflare blocks my automated browser.
3. Then I flip `MALUDB_SIGNUPS_OPEN` to true as the last change.

I'd also like to delete the walkthrough project `3u2rzs6e` once #226 is deployed, as the first real use of the new path.

## 🤖 Claude

Confirmed clean on the node — no database, no roles, and the record reads DELETED. But the **storage worker still holds the deleted tenant's registration**, which includes its database URL and JWT secret. That's the ADR-085 gap: the worker's admin port is on the node's loopback, so the control plane can't reach it.

Removing that registration by hand now, from the node.

<details><summary>🔧 Bash</summary>

```json

  "command": "ssh -i ~/.ssh/maludb_rehearsal maludb@10.120.0.172 'cd /; KEY=$(sudo grep -o \"^SERVER_ADMIN_API_KEYS=.*\" /etc/maludb/storage/storage.env | cut -d= -f2); curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"deregister 3u2rzs6e: %{http_code}\\n\" -X DELETE -H \"apikey: $KEY\" http://127.0.0.1:5001/tenants/3u2rzs6e; curl -s -H \"apikey: $KEY\" http://127.0.0.1:5001/tenants | python3 -c \"import json,sys; print(\\\"tenants now:\\\", [t[\\\"id\\\"] for t in json.load(sys.stdin)])\"'",

  "timeout": 120000
}

## 🤖 Claude

#226 is deployed to both VMs (main 7d52e49, migration 0060 applied), and I used it for real: **the walkthrough project is gone** — database dropped, 6 roles removed, its uploaded file deleted from the bucket, and the record kept as DELETED so the reference is never reissued.

**Preflight now exits 2 with no failures.** The only two warnings are artefacts of running it with the provisioner's environment: it can't check the gateway role from the control plane, and it doesn't see the console's bind setting in that file.

**One finding from using it, and it must be fixed before signups open.** Deleting a project **couldn't deregister the shared storage worker**, because that worker's admin API listens on the node's loopback and the control plane can't reach it — the gap ADR-085 already noted. What it leaves behind is the deleted tenant's **database URL and JWT secret** in the worker's metadata, pointing at a database that no longer exists. I removed this one by hand on the node, but every future deletion would leave one.

I've recorded it as **slice 10c** in PR #227 (docs only), with the two options:
- a node-side reconciliation of the worker's tenant list, which keeps that admin port off the network as ADR-085 intended;
- or admitting the control plane to that port, the way ADR-085 already admits it to S3.

I'd build the first. Note for whoever does: deletion clears `node_id`, so the node's own role can't see the deleted row afterwards — the instruction has to be recorded rather than inferred.

**Where the free tier stands**
- **Done:** slices 1–10b, all deployed and verified on test.maludb.org.
- **Mine:** slice 10c.
- **Yours:** the legal answers I emailed to jlehman@kineticseas.com, the support/security/abuse addresses, and one browser signup by hand.
- **Last step, when you say so:** flipping signups on.

## 🤖 Claude

No migration needed for 10c, which is better: the node's gateway role already sees **only its own node's live projects** through row-level security (ADR-072). So a node-side reconciler can ask "which of the refs the worker holds are still live here?" and deregister the rest — deleted projects and ones moved away both disappear from that view. Building it.

def deregister_tenant(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, project_ref: str) -> None:
    """Remove a tenant from the shared worker.

    A 404 is success: the goal is that the worker does not serve this tenant,
    and a worker that has never heard of it already meets that.
    """
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise StorageWorkerError(f"invalid project ref {project_ref!r}")
    _admin(
        "DELETE",
        f"/tenants/{project_ref}",
        admin_port=admin_port,
        api_key=api_key,
        expect_missing_ok=True,
    )


def tenant_known(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, project_ref: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the worker currently holds a configuration for this tenant.

    Presence, and nothing else. The admin API answers this with the tenant's
    **whole** configuration -- its database URL, which carries a live password,
    and its JWT signing secret -- so the body is discarded here rather than
    returned. A caller that never receives it cannot log it, which is the same
    rule `_admin` follows for error bodies and for the same reason.

    A 404 is the answer this exists to get: it is what a worker whose
    multitenant database was rebuilt says about a tenant the control plane
    believes it serves.
    """
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise StorageWorkerError(f"invalid project ref {project_ref!r}")
    found = _admin(
        "GET",
        f"/tenants/{project_ref}",
        admin_port=admin_port,
        api_key=api_key,
        expect_missing_ok=True,
    )
    return found is not None


def is_ready(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, timeout: float = 2.0) -> bool:
    """Whether the worker is up and has migrated its multitenant database.

    Asks a question only a migrated instance can answer, rather than checking
    that a port is open: the container accepts connections before it has run its
    own migrations, and a readiness check that a half-started worker passes is
    how a tenant gets registered into a database that has no table for it.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

def _admin(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    *,
    admin_port: int,
    api_key: str,
    payload: dict | None = None,
    expect_missing_ok: bool = False,
) -> dict | None:
    """One call to the worker's admin API, on loopback.

    The credential goes in an **`apikey`** header. `Authorization` answers 401,
    which slice 0 recorded because it costs an hour to discover and reads like a
    wrong key rather than a wrong header.
    """
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{admin_port}{path}"
    try:
        response = httpx.request(
            method,
            url,
            headers={"apikey": api_key, "content-type": "application/json"},
            content=json.dumps(payload) if payload is not None else None,
            timeout=ADMIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
        )
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        # Never the exception's text: a transport error can echo the URL, and
        # the URL is harmless but the habit is worth keeping consistent.
        raise StorageWorkerError(
            f"the storage worker's admin API did not answer ({type(exc).__name__})"
        ) from None

    if expect_missing_ok and response.status_code == 404:
        return None
    if response.status_code >= 400:
        # The body can carry a tenant's configuration; the status alone is what
        # a caller needs and what a log should hold.
        raise StorageWorkerError(
            f"the storage worker's admin API answered {response.status_code} to {method} {path}"
        )
    if not response.content:
        return {}
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError:
        return {}


def tenant_payload(
    *,
    project_ref: str,
    tenant_dsn: str,
    jwt_secret: str,
    database_pool_size: int,
) -> dict:
    """What the admin API is told about one tenant.

    The DSN and the JWT secret are the whole of it, and both are the platform's
    own: the customer never supplies either. `jwtSecret` is the project's own
    signing secret, shared with PostgREST and GoTrue -- a second secret here
    would make every token the gateway accepts fail at the Storage API.
    """
    return {
        "anonKey": "",
        "serviceKey": "",
        "jwtSecret": jwt_secret,
        "databaseUrl": tenant_dsn,
        "databasePoolUrl": tenant_dsn,
        "maxConnections": database_pool_size,
----
def deregister_tenant(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, project_ref: str) -> None:
    """Remove a tenant from the shared worker.

    A 404 is success: the goal is that the worker does not serve this tenant,
    and a worker that has never heard of it already meets that.
    """
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise StorageWorkerError(f"invalid project ref {project_ref!r}")
    _admin(
        "DELETE",
        f"/tenants/{project_ref}",
        admin_port=admin_port,
        api_key=api_key,
        expect_missing_ok=True,
    )


def tenant_known(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, project_ref: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the worker currently holds a configuration for this tenant.

    Presence, and nothing else. The admin API answers this with the tenant's
    **whole** configuration -- its database URL, which carries a live password,
    and its JWT signing secret -- so the body is discarded here rather than
    returned. A caller that never receives it cannot log it, which is the same
    rule `_admin` follows for error bodies and for the same reason.

    A 404 is the answer this exists to get: it is what a worker whose
    multitenant database was rebuilt says about a tenant the control plane
    believes it serves.
    """
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise StorageWorkerError(f"invalid project ref {project_ref!r}")
    found = _admin(
        "GET",
        f"/tenants/{project_ref}",
        admin_port=admin_port,
        api_key=api_key,
        expect_missing_ok=True,
    )
    return found is not None


def known_tenants(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str) -> tup

---
# The node's half of the maintenance pass (ADR-083), run by maludb-node-maintenance.timer.
#
# Sleeps this node's idle PostgREST, GoTrue and Realtime workers -- ADR-022's free-tier density. It
# runs **as maludb-gateway with the gateway's own database role**, which already reads and updates
# this node's worker state and may stop exactly those units (deploy/50-maludb-gateway.rules).
#
# **No KEK, no pepper.** Unlike the gateway's unit there is no LoadCredential here; the node pass
# reads MALUDB_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL from gateway.env and nothing else it holds.
# `tests/test_deploy_units.py` asserts both.

[Unit]
Description=MaluDB maintenance pass (node: sleep idle workers)
Documentation=file:///opt/maludb/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=maludb-gateway
Group=maludb-gateway
EnvironmentFile=/etc/maludb/gateway.env
ExecStart=/opt/maludb/.venv/bin/python -m services.control_plane.node_maintenance
WorkingDirectory=/opt/maludb
TimeoutStartSec=5min

NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectSystem=strict
# tmpfs, not true: libpq looks for ~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt on every TLS
# connection and tolerates ENOENT but not the EACCES that `true` returns.
ProtectHome=tmpfs
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
ReadOnlyPaths=/opt/maludb /etc/maludb
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX
RestrictNamespaces=true

# The per-object ceiling handed to the worker when a tenant is registered.
#
# **Not zero.** `fileSizeLimit: 0` reads like "no limit" and means a limit of
# zero bytes: every upload answers `413 EntityTooLarge`, which was the first
# thing the end-to-end spike found. There is no sentinel for unlimited, so this
# is a real number and it is deliberately generous -- 50 GiB, above anything a
# plan will allow.
#
# The ceiling a customer actually meets is their plan's `object_storage_bytes`
# (ADR-056), enforced by the gateway in slice 4. This one exists so that a
# request which somehow reached the worker without passing the gateway is still
# bounded by something, in the same spirit as Realtime's `MAX_CONNECTIONS`.
TENANT_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT = 50 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024

def register_tenant(
    *,
    admin_port: int,
    api_key: str,
    project_ref: str,
    tenant_dsn: str,
    jwt_secret: str,
    database_pool_size: int = 5,
) -> None:
    """Tell the shared worker about one tenant. Idempotent.

    **PUT, not POST, and the difference is not stylistic.** Upstream offers
    both on `/tenants/{id}`: `POST` inserts and answers `500` with a primary key
    violation if the tenant is already there, while `PUT` calls its
    `upsertTenantAndGenerateJwk` and rewrites the configuration. Measured, by
    writing `POST` here first and watching the second provisioning run of the
    same project fail.

    That makes the whole retry story work: this is safe on a provisioning
    retry, safe to re-run when a plan changes the pool size, and safe to run for
    every project on a node when a worker is rebuilt.
    """
    if not models.is_valid_project_ref(project_ref):
        raise StorageWorkerError(f"invalid project ref {project_ref!r}")
    _admin(
        "PUT",
        f"/tenants/{project_ref}",
        admin_port=admin_port,
        api_key=api_key,
        payload=tenant_payload(
            project_ref=project_ref,
            tenant_dsn=tenant_dsn,
            jwt_secret=jwt_secret,
            database_pool_size=database_pool_size,
        ),
    )

def is_ready(*, admin_port: int, api_key: str, timeout: float = 2.0) -> bool:
    """Whether the worker is up and has migrated its multitenant database.

    Asks a question only a migrated instance can answer, rather than checking
    that a port is open: the container accepts connections before it has run its
    own migrations, and a readiness check that a half-started worker passes is
    how a tenant gets registered into a database that has no table for it.
    """
    try:
        response = httpx.get(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{admin_port}/tenants",
            headers={"apikey": api_key},
            timeout=timeout,
        )
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        return False
    return response.status_code == 200

# than PostgREST and faster than Realtime's BEAM.
READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60.0
READINESS_POLL_SECONDS = 0.5
ADMIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15.0

# The per-object ceiling handed to the worker when a tenant is registered.
#
# **Not zero.** `fileSizeLimit: 0` reads like "no limit" and means a limit of
# zero bytes: every upload answers `413 EntityTooLarge`, which was the first
# thing the end-to-end spike found. There is no sentinel for unlimited, so this
# is a real number and it is deliberately generous -- 50 GiB, above anything a
# plan will allow.
#
# The ceiling a customer actually meets is their plan's `object_storage_bytes`
# (ADR-056), enforced by the gateway in slice 4. This one exists so that a
# request which somehow reached the worker without passing the gateway is still
# bounded by something, in the same spirit as Realtime's `MAX_CONNECTIONS`.
TENANT_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT = 50 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024

<details><summary>🔧 Write</summary>

```json
{
  "file_path": "/home/maludb/mpa-10c/services/control_plane/node_storage.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"The node's storage reconciler: nothing registered for a project the node no longer serves.\n\nFree slice 10c, found deploying project deletion (10b). `jobs.delete_project` drops the tenant's\ndatabase, roles and objects, but it cannot deregister the shared `storage-api` worker: that worker's\nadmin API listens on the **node's** loopback and the control plane is another machine -- ADR-085 put\nit there deliberately, because that API can rewrite any tenant's database URL. So a deleted project\nleft a registration behind carrying its database URL and its JWT signing secret, naming a database\nthat no longer exists.\n\nThis closes it from the node, where that port is reachable:\n\n    python -m services.control_plane.node_storage reconcile\n\n**No KEK and no new database role.** The worker's admin credential is already on the node, in the\nenvironment file the worker itself reads, and systemd hands this pass the two values it needs from\nthat file. *Which projects this node still serves* is a question the gateway's own role can answer\non its own, because ADR-072's row policies show that role exactly its own node's projects: a project\nthat was deleted, or moved to another node, simply stops being visible -- which is the same answer\nas \"this node should not be serving it\". Like `node_maintenance`, this imports nothing that can\nreach the key ring, and `tests/test_node_storage.py` walks the closure to keep it so.\n\n**It fails closed.** If the control plane cannot be asked, or the worker's listing cannot be read,\nthe pass deregisters nothing and exits non-zero. The risk worth being careful about is not a stale\nregistration -- it is this pass concluding, from a bad answer, that a live tenant should stop being\nserved, which would take that project's Storage API down until someone noticed.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport psycopg\n\nfrom services.control_plane import logging as cp_logging\nfrom services.control_plane import storage_admin\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# A bound on how much one pass may undo. Deregistering is cheap to repeat and expensive to get wrong\n# in bulk, so a pass wanting to remove more than this says so and removes nothing. The shape it\n# guards against is not \"many deletions on a busy day\" -- it is the gateway role losing its node\n# mapping, in which case ADR-072's policies correctly answer \"no projects\" and every tenant on the\n# node looks stale at once. Fifty is far above a day's deletions and far below a node's population.\nMAX_DEREGISTRATIONS = 50\n\n\nclass ReconcileRefused(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"The pass will not act on the answer it got.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef live_refs(conn: psycopg.Connection, candidates: tuple[str, ...]) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"Which of these refs are projects this node still serves, as the database will say.\n\n    The connection is the gateway's own role, so ADR-072's row policies answer for this node and no\n    other. `delete_project` clears the placement, so a deleted project is not visible here even\n    while its row remains -- which is what makes a deleted tenant reconcilable at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not candidates:\n        return set()\n    with conn.cursor() as cursor:\n        cursor.execute(\n            \"SELECT project_ref FROM projects WHERE project_ref = ANY(%s)\",\n            (list(candidates),),\n        )\n        return {row[0] for row in cursor.fetchall()}\n\n\ndef reconcile(\n    *,\n    database_url: str,\n    admin_port: int,\n    api_key: str,\n    connect=psycopg.connect,\n    admin=storage_admin,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Deregister every tenant this node no longer serves. Returns how many were removed.\"\"\"\n    registered = admin.known_tenants(admin_port=admin_port, api_key=api_key)\n    if not registered:\n        log.info(\"the storage worker holds no tenants; nothing to reconcile\")\n        return 0\n\n    # A short connection, opened for this question and closed before anything is changed: the same\n    # shape `node_backup` uses, so a slow deregistration does not hold a control-plane connection.\n    with connect(database_url, connect_timeout=10) as conn:\n        live = live_refs(conn, registered)\n\n    stale = sorted(set(registered) - live)\n    if not stale:\n        log.info(\"every registered tenant is a project this node serves (%d)\", len(registered))\n        return 0\n    if len(stale) > MAX_DEREGISTRATIONS:\n        raise ReconcileRefused(\n            f\"{len(stale)} of {len(registered)} registered tenants look stale, over the limit of \"\n            f\"{MAX_DEREGISTRATIONS}. That is the shape of a wrong answer rather than that many \"\n            f\"deletions -- check that this node's gateway role is still mapped to this node. \"\n            f\"Nothing was deregistered\"\n        )\n\n    removed = 0\n    for ref in stale:\n        try:\n            admin.deregister_tenant(admin_port=admin_port, api_key=api_key, project_ref=ref)\n        except storage_admin.StorageWorkerError as exc:\n            # One tenant's failure is not the next one's: the pass is idempotent and runs again.\n            log.warning(\"could not deregister %s (%s)\", ref, exc)\n            continue\n        removed += 1\n        log.info(\"deregistered %s: this node no longer serves it\", ref)\n    return removed\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"node_storage\", description=__doc__.split(\"\\n\\n\")[0])\n    parser.add_argument(\"command\", choices=(\"reconcile\",))\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    cp_logging.configure()\n    assert args.command == \"reconcile\"  # noqa: S101 - argparse has already refused anything else\n\n    database_url = os.environ.get(\"MALUDB_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL\", \"\").strip()\n    # `SERVER_ADMIN_API_KEYS` and `MALUDB_STORAGE_ADMIN_HOST_PORT` are the worker's own names, read\n    # from the worker's own environment file by systemd. Naming them again here would be a second\n    # copy of a credential, and a second copy is a thing that drifts.\n    api_key = os.environ.get(\"SERVER_ADMIN_API_KEYS\", \"\").strip()\n    port = os.environ.get(\"MALUDB_STORAGE_ADMIN_HOST_PORT\", \"\").strip()\n    missing = [\n        name for name, value in (\n            (\"MALUDB_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL\", database_url),\n            (\"SERVER_ADMIN_API_KEYS\", api_key),\n            (\"MALUDB_STORAGE_ADMIN_HOST_PORT\", port),\n        ) if not value\n    ]\n    if missing:\n        raise SystemExit(\n            f\"missing {', '.join(missing)}: this pass reads the gateway's database URL from \"\n            f\"gateway.env and the worker's admin address from the worker's own storage.env\"\n        )\n    if not port.isdigit():\n        raise SystemExit(f\"MALUDB_STORAGE_ADMIN_HOST_PORT is not a port number: {port!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        removed = reconcile(database_url=database_url, admin_port=int(port), api_key=api_key)\n    except (storage_admin.StorageWorkerError, ReconcileRefused) as exc:\n        log.error(\"reconcile: %s\", exc)\n        return 1\n    except psycopg.Error as exc:\n        # The server's message, never the exception's text: a connection error echoes the DSN.\n        primary = (exc.diag.message_primary or \"\").strip() if exc.diag else \"\"\n        log.error(\"reconcile: could not ask the control plane (%s%s)\",\n                  type(exc).__name__, f\": {primary}\" if primary else \"\")\n        return 1\n    log.info(\"reconcile finished: %d tenant(s) deregistered\", removed)\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}

"""The maintenance pass, split (ADR-083).

The node half runs **as a real gateway role** against two nodes, because the property that
matters is what that role can and cannot do rather than what the code intends:

- it sleeps its own node's idle workers and marks them stopped, and nothing on another node;
- it records its runs for its own node, and cannot record or read one for another;
- the gateway role cannot touch `maintenance_runs`, which preflight trusts for the control plane;
- a role that is no node's gateway sleeps nothing;
- the module reaches no key ring, node credential or provisioning code.

The control-plane half: `run_all(skip=...)` does not call a skipped pass at all.
"""

class FakeSupervisor:
    def __init__(self, fail: set[str] | None = None):
        self.stopped: list[str] = []
        self.fail = fail or set()

    def start(self, project_ref):  # pragma: no cover - not used by the pass
        raise AssertionError("the node pass never starts a worker")

    def stop(self, project_ref):
        if project_ref in self.fail:
            raise supervision.WorkerError(f"could not stop {project_ref}")
        self.stopped.append(project_ref)

    def is_active(self, project_ref):  # pragma: no cover
        return True

def _as_role(role: str):
    """A connection that is the gateway role for its whole life, commits included."""
    with psycopg.connect(DATABASE_URL, row_factory=dict_row) as conn:
        conn.execute(f'SET ROLE "{role}"')
        conn.commit()
        try:
            yield conn
        finally:
            conn.rollback()

import os
import socket

import pytest

DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get("MALUDB_CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL", "").strip()


def _resolves(hostname: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a compatibility suite's project hostname is in /etc/hosts.

    Here rather than only in the suites themselves because the banner has to
    say what did not run, and a suite that skipped cannot say it.
    """
    try:
        socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None)
    except socket.gaierror:
        return False
    return True

requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(not DATABASE_URL, reason="MALUDB_CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL is unset")

**On the node** -- start both, then tell the gateway Storage exists:

```bash
sudo cp deploy/maludb-object-store.service deploy/maludb-storage.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now maludb-object-store
sudo nft list table inet maludb_object_store >/dev/null && echo firewall loaded

sudo systemctl enable --now maludb-storage
journalctl -u maludb-storage -f                 # until it logs that it is listening

sudoedit /etc/maludb/gateway.env    # MALUDB_STORAGE_DB_HOST=10.91.0.1, MALUDB_STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT=http://NODE:8333
sudo systemctl restart maludb-gateway
```

Then `cp-manage deploy preflight` on the control plane, **with `provisioner.env` loaded**: "object store" passes when the bucket answers
from there and every active node has a sealed storage root. From anywhere else on the private network
`curl http://NODE:8333/` must time out.

**What this does not give you.** The store keeps **one copy** of every object on the node's disk
(SeaweedFS replication `000`). ADR-069 counts that a production failure; `cp-manage storage
durability` cannot see the master from the control plane and reports it as undeclared. Until the
backup slice covers the store, a lost disk loses customers' files outright. And the maintenance
pass's `storage_tenants` reconciliation needs the worker's admin port on node loopback, so from the
control plane it reports "not ready" and does nothing; a worker that loses its metadata database is
repaired by hand, not by the pass (ADR-085).

### 2.8 Backups: the node's recorder role (ADR-086)

pgBackRest runs on the node, as `postgres`, and records what it did through a role that can call
three functions for its own node and nothing else (`start_node_backup`, `finish_node_backup`,
`record_node_backup_check`) -- the health reporter's pattern (§2.5). The node holds no KEK and no
control-plane role that can write a table.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
for p in "$@"; do
  while true; do
    total=$(gh pr view "$p" --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup | length')
    pending=$(gh pr view "$p" --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.status != "COMPLETED")] | length')
    if [ "$total" -gt 1 ] && [ "$pending" = 0 ]; then break; fi
    sleep 20
  done
  bad=$(gh pr view "$p" --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.conclusion != "SUCCESS")] | length')
  if [ "$bad" != 0 ]; then echo "$p checks NOT green"; continue; fi
  gh pr merge "$p" --merge >/dev/null 2>&1 || { sleep 25; gh pr merge "$p" --merge >/dev/null 2>&1; }
  sleep 5
  echo "$p $(gh pr view "$p" --json state --jq .state)"
done

    conn: psycopg.Connection,
    *,
    node_id: int,
    key_ring: crypto.KeyRing,
    config,

    metadata_connect,
) -> StorageSettings:
    """Everything the control plane owes a node before its worker can start.

    Run from the control plane, because it is the one place holding all three
    things this needs: write access to `nodes` to seal the root (which the
    gateway is refused on purpose), the node's admin credential for the
    multitenant database, and the object-store credential. Nothing on the node
    holds more than one of them.

    Idempotent: the root is sealed once and reused, the role's password is re-set
    to the value it already derives to, and the database is created only if
    absent. The configuration is checked *before* anything is sealed or created,
    so a control plane missing `MALUDB_STORAGE_*` fails without leaving a node
    with a root and no worker.

## 🤖 Claude

Both merged and built:

**#227 merged** — the plan entry recording the storage-deregistration gap.

**Slice 10c built, PR #228 open** — a deleted tenant now leaves nothing on the node.

The shape of it: a hourly node-side pass (`node_storage reconcile`) running as `maludb-gateway`. It asks the worker what tenants it holds, asks the control plane which of those this node still serves, and deregisters the rest. No new database role, no migration, no opening of the admin port.

Two things worth flagging:

**The plan's worry was actually the mechanism.** The entry said that because `delete_project` clears `node_id`, the gateway can no longer see the deleted row — so the deregistration would have to be *recorded* as work. It's the opposite: ADR-072's policies key on `node_id`, so clearing it makes the project invisible to exactly the role doing the reconciling, and "the worker holds a ref this node can't see" already means "remove it." That also covers a project moved to another node, which a queued instruction wouldn't have.

**I fixed one finding in my own draft before committing.** The obvious unit took the admin credential from the worker's `storage.env` via `EnvironmentFile`. That file also holds `AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and the multitenant database URL — between them every tenant's Storage credentials on the node — plus the object store's secret key. A process environment is readable by any process of the same user, so that would have handed all of it to `maludb-gateway` once an hour to save writing a file. Narrowed to a two-value `reconcile.env`, rendered by the same `storage-prepare` run so the two can't drift.

Also split the admin API into `storage_admin`, a leaf importing only `httpx` and `models`, so this node-side pass can't reach the key ring — `node_maintenance`'s rule, asserted by an import-closure walk. All names re-exported; no caller changed.

It fails closed throughout: an unreachable control plane or an unreadable listing deregisters nothing, and more than 50 stale refs in one pass is refused and named, since that's the shape of a gateway role that lost its node mapping.

22 new tests pass locally, including the RLS assertions against a real gateway role. Full suite and CI are running; I'll merge #228 when it's green — say the word and I'll deploy it to the rehearsal node, where the by-hand deregistration from the 10b drill means there should be nothing left for the first pass to find.

One local note: your test database needed two fixes to run the gateway-role tests at all — four tables were owned by `cp_ci` rather than `cp_dev`, and `cp_dev` lacked `CREATEROLE` plus `createrole_self_grant = 'set'`. Those tests were silently skipping before. I changed the dev cluster, not the repo.

## 🤖 Claude

Status on the two things you asked for:

**#227 — merged.** Confirmed on `origin/main`.

**10c — built, PR #228 open**, CI running.

The reconciler runs hourly on the node as `maludb-gateway`: it asks the storage worker what tenants it holds, asks the control plane which of those the node still serves, and deregisters the rest. No new role, no migration, and the admin port stays off the network.

The plan entry predicted this would need the deregistration *recorded* as work, because `delete_project` clears `node_id` and hides the row from the gateway. That turned out to be the mechanism rather than the obstacle — ADR-072's policies key on `node_id`, so a ref the worker holds that the gateway cannot see is definitionally one this node shouldn't serve. It also picks up projects moved to another node, which a queued instruction wouldn't.

I caught and fixed one issue in my own first draft: the unit read the worker's `storage.env`, which carries `AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, the multitenant DB URL and the object store's secret — every tenant's Storage credentials on that node — and a process environment is readable by any process of the same user. Narrowed to a two-value `reconcile.env` rendered by the same `storage-prepare` command. Also split the admin API into a leaf module so node-side code can't reach the key ring, asserted by an import-closure walk.

**On the local suite:** 1774 passed, but 3 failed and 6 errored. The errors reproduce identically on unmodified `main` — they're tests that were silently *skipping* until I granted `cp_dev` CREATEROLE, and now fail because `MALUDB_NODE_ADMIN_DSN` is unset on this box. I'm re-running with full output to identify the 3 failures rather than assume they're the same category; I'll confirm against `main` before claiming they're unrelated, and won't ask you to merge #228 until I have.

Two things for you when convenient:

- Your test database had four tables owned by `cp_ci` instead of `cp_dev`, and `cp_dev` lacked CREATEROLE — so the gateway-role RLS tests have been skipping locally. I fixed the cluster, not the repo. Setting `MALUDB_NODE_ADMIN_DSN` against a disposable cluster would un-skip the rest, but that creates and drops `mldb_*` roles and databases, so I've left it for you to decide.
- Deploy of 10c to the rehearsal node needs your go-ahead. The by-hand deregistration you did during the 10b drill means the first pass should find nothing — a clean way to see it report `0 tenant(s) deregistered` before it ever has real work.

That's the failure mode AGENTS.md is emphatic about getting right, just inverted — noisy rather than silent. ## 🤖 Claude

The local suite finished, and the answer changed: **there were only ever 2 real failures.**

```
2 failed, 1774 passed, 618 skipped, 5 errors in 614s
```

Both are the GoTrue ones I already traced to a missing binary, reproduced on unmodified `main`. The five `test_extension_upgrade` errors are the same category — they need `MALUDB_NODE_ADMIN_DSN`, which this box doesn't have.

The third failure from the first run was **my own fault, not the code's**. I had started that full suite in the background and then kept running targeted suites against the same test database while it was going. Two pytest processes truncating tables and creating roles concurrently deadlocked on `pg_class` — I saw that deadlock in a targeted run and stopped the background suite, but the damage was already recorded in its count. A clean serial run shows 2. Nothing from slice 10c.

So the local picture is clean. Worth my remembering not to overlap runs against one test database — the failure it produces looks like a real bug and costs a ten-minute re-run to disprove.

CI `check` on #228 is still pending; the merge watcher is armed and will only fire on all-green. Deploy scripts are staged and both hosts are clean at 7d52e49. I'll report the merge and then the deploy result — including whatever number the first reconcile pass actually prints, rather than the zero I expect.

## 🤖 Claude

**#228 merged (`bb08ce3`) and deployed. Verified working, not just installed.**

Both hosts fast-forwarded, `reconcile.env` piped host-to-host into `/etc/maludb/storage/reconcile.env` (root 0600, exactly two keys, never through a terminal), unit and timer installed and armed — next run 00:13 UTC, hourly after that.

The proof, in three passes:

1. **First pass:** `every registered tenant is a project this node serves (1)` → 0 deregistered. Correct, and it also settles the earlier confusion — `GET /tenants` answered 200, so my original 404 really was a bad probe hitting port 80.
2. **Planted a departed tenant** (`zzzztest`, a ref no project owns, dummy DSN, unreachable through the gateway): present 200 → pass runs → **404**, journal says `deregistered zzzztest: this node no longer serves it`, `1 tenant(s) deregistered`.
3. **Ran it again:** back to 0, live tenant untouched.

I did this with a planted registration rather than by provisioning and deleting a real project — same code path, no 208-second provision and no destruction of anything real.

**One thing the test surfaced that's worth your judgement.** My first attempt used `zzzz0test` — nine characters. The pass silently ignored it, because `known_tenants` drops anything that isn't a valid 8-character project ref before it can reach a URL path. That filter is right (the listing comes out of the worker's own database and AGENTS.md treats refs as untrusted), but the consequence is that a malformed registration is invisible to the reconciler *forever* — it can never be swept up, only removed by hand, which is what I did to clean up.

Nothing can currently create such a registration: `register_tenant` validates the ref on the way in, so the only source would be direct admin-API access or a corrupted metadata database. So it's a latent gap rather than a live one. The honest options are to leave it (and note it), or to have the pass count and log refs it had to skip so they're at least visible. I'd lean to the latter — one log line, no new behaviour — but it's a separate change and I'd rather ask than fold it into a merged slice.

Free-tier remaining: H-4 legal placeholders and H-6 addresses (both yours), one manual browser signup, then flipping `MALUDB_SIGNUPS_OPEN`.
